gloss: Connective: sumti afterthought or

meaning.exp: Logical connective: sumti afterthought or. Connects two sumti, such that the containing bridi is true if and only if it is true for at least one of the connected sumti.
meaning.note: Supplanted with {{ja}} in JACU.

example.lojban: .i xu mi klama lo mu'a ceizda {{.a}} lo mu'a pacraistu
example.english: Do I go to, say, heaven {{or}} hell?
example.author: Andy Weir

meaning.exp: Letteral for a. When used alone, refers to the most recent sumti starting with {{a}}.

example.lojban: .i ro da sutra fa'a {{la .alis.}} ca lo nu {{.a bu}} tolcanci
example.english: They all made a rush at {{Alice}} the moment {{she}} (= Alice) appeared.
example.author: Lewis Carroll

meaning.exp: Equivalent to {{.i pau}}. Starts a sentence that is by default a question.
meaning.note: Adopting ajbo prerequires adopting JACU. A sentence started with {{.a}} always contains a question marker ({{xu}}, {{ma}}, {{mo}} etc.)

example.lojban: {{.a xu}} do pu zi mo'u gunka tu'a lo do jibri
example.english: Did you just finished your job{{?}}
example.speaker: la srasu

example.lojban: {{.anai}} la loglan cu jbobau {{xu}} .i na go'i ni'i loka lujvo {{.a xu}} ku'i la loglan cu lojbo bangu
example.english: Is Loglan Lojban{{?}} It's not because of the lujvo [structure]. But is Loglan some kind of Lojban-ic language{{?}}
example.speaker: la melmi
example.note: The first sentence seems to be a question where the speaker is asking themselves or is expecting a negative answer, but it's hard to say for sure because there are no other instances of {{.anai}} in similar usage.

meaning.exp: Starts a response to a question.

example.lojban:
— .i nancaji li xo
— {{.anai}} reze
example.english:
— How old are you (in years)?
— Twenty-seven.
example.speaker: la nonselcme, la srasu
example.note: The former sentence is compatible with CLL Lojban. The latter is in ajbo.

meaning.exp: Starts a rhetorical question.
meaning.note: This meaning is only attested once, making it a hapax. This usage is listed separately because this usage is mentioned (but not used) by other speakers.

example.lojban: {{.anai}} la catra cu catra xu zo'o
example.english: Does "Killer" kill{{? /j}}
example.note: This is the only instance of {{.a nai}} being used as a rhetorical question starter.
example.speaker: .kúblizel.

gloss: Attitudinal: intention — indicision/hesitation — refusal

meaning.exp: Attitudinal: express intent / purpose / design.

example.lojban: .i {{.ai}} mi ba snada ro se troci
example.english: I{{'ll}} succeed in every one of my goal.
example.author: Djemynai

meaning.exp: Attitudinal: express indecision / hesitation / vacillation / wavering.

example.lojban: ― .i pu zi co'i mo'u tinzga 100 zo'e .ibo ca surla .i {{.aicu'i}} tinzga lo velvi'u 400mei
example.english: ― Just finished listening to the first 100 and am now taking a break. {{Unsure if}} I'll listen to the remaining 400.
example.speaker: la lalxu

meaning.exp: Attitudinal: express rejection / refusal.

example.lojban: .i go pu'o zei ganlo se morji gi ne'i la'e di'u milxe bacru za'a sei {{.ai nai}} tolmo'i
example.english: The unclosed memories, I hear whispers inside them that {{we never want to}} forget.
example.author: Youmi Kimura

meaning.exp: Attitudinal: express unintention / accidentiality.
meaning.note: Unattested.

gloss: Attitudinal: hope — despair

meaning.exp: Attitudinal: express hope / longing.

example.lojban: .i a'o ro da zabna
example.english: {{I hope}} everything is good.
example.author: la .cogas.

meaning.exp: Attitudinal: express despair / hopelessness / dread / fear.

example.lojban: .i le trene pu zi co'a cliva se ka'a lo tcadu poi darno {{.a'o nai}}
example.english: The train's just started to leave for the faraway city, {{oh no...}}
example.author: inabakumori

meaning.exp: Attitudinal: express hope/longing that the opposite is true.

example.lojban: .i ra'apxu co zabnytce .i ti zabna bangu .i .ai mi xabju pe'a .i ta'o xu xekce {{.a'o nai}} .ie'i
example.english: It's a really nice rap. This is a nice language, I wanna live in it. BTW, is it xekce ({{I hope not}}, eww)?
example.speaker: la lunbe

gloss: Attitudinal: interest — disinterest/indifference — repulsion

meaning.exp: Attitudinal: express interest / curiosity / concern / preoccupation.

example.lojban: .i {{.a'u sai}} .i ti lo nu mi sipna cu fanmo
example.english: {{Cool,}} this is the end of my sleep.
example.author: Djemynai

meaning.exp: Attitudinal: express disinterest / uninterest / unconcern / apathy / detachment / indifference.

example.lojban: {{.a'ucu'i}} .i ka'u mi'o na ba se fatri lo do'anai bongu .oi
example.english: {{Whatever.}} Now we won't be served anything, not even bones...
example.author: Kenji Miyazawa

meaning.exp: Attitudinal: express repulsion / aversion / disgust / distaste / repugnance.

example.lojban: {{.a'u nai}} bu'o pilno lo do voksa
example.english: I {{don't want to}} use your voice anymore!
example.author: ryo

gloss: Preposition (tense): after ...; future tense

meaning.exp: Future: signifies the event happens / the proposition holds at some point after the reference point.
meaning.note: When used alone in main clauses, the reference point is usually that of the speaker, which makes {{ba}} function like a future tense marker. In subordinate clauses, the reference point is the point in spacetime at which the outer clause takes place. Note that {{ba}} alone says nothing about whether the sentence is true now or in the past.

example.lojban: mi {{ba}} citka ma
example.english: What {{will}} I eat…?
example.author: la lalxu

example.lojban: ni'o {{ba ku}} lo cmalu noltru cu junri te pinka
example.english: {{Then}} the little prince said, earnestly,
example.note: This sentence is in the "narrative tense," in which the reference point is the time within the story itself. Thus, {{ba ku}} is taken to be the future relative to the events described in the previous sentences, thus its translation of "then". Note that the {{ku}} cannot be elided in this sentence, or the {{ba}} will take {{lo cmalu noltru}} as its reference point.
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

example.lojban: doi ga'i nai noltru mi'a pu jinvi lo du'u do {{ba}} se catra
example.english: Oh, your Majesty, we thought you {{would}} be killed!
example.note: This is an example of a {{ba}} inside a subordinate clause that expresses a tense relative to the main clause. Since the main clause is in the past tense, the {{ba}} creates the effect of "future-in-the-past." The event expressed by the subordinate clause is still in the past, though later in time than the event expressed by the main clause, according to the context.
example.author: L. Frank Baum

meaning.exp: Specifies the reference point to be the attached sumti. Essentially means "after ...".

example.lojban: .i ro da {{ba}} lo nu .a bu limna lo lalxu cu simlu lo ka ba'o cenba
example.english: Everything seemed to have changed {{since}} her swim in the pool.
example.author: Lewis Carroll

meaning.exp: Specifies the time distance to the reference point to be the attached sumti.
meaning.note: Using {{se}} with {{ba}} isn't permitted in CLL Lojban, but is permitted in camxes beta, camxes experimental and zantufa.

example.lojban: .i mi kansa {{seba lo mentu be li ji'i reno}}
example.english: I {{will}} be with [you] {{in about twenty minutes}}.
example.speaker: Lucilla

gloss: Emphasize next word

meaning.exp: Forethought emphasis indicator: Indicates that next word is especially emphasized or emphatic.
meaning.note: For grammatical purposes, {{ba'e}} marks the following word but does not change its nature. (The construct behaves just as the marked word by itself.) Multiple BAhE cmavo may be used in succession, and they combine to mark the next non-BAhE word.

example.lojban: .i ja'o mi bilga lo nu jmina finti {{ba'e so}} lo tricu
example.english: So I have to create {{nine}} more trees to add.
example.author: Worldbuilding Notes

example.lojban: .e'e ju'o ca le {{ba'e ca}} jeftu mi roldei tcidu ro se ciska be ro le mi jbope'o
example.english: {{This}} week, I definitely can read every day what all my Lojban friends have written!
example.speaker: latkerlo

example.lojban: .i xu {{ba'e do}} nelci lo mlatu va'o lo nu da'i do me mi
example.english: Would {{you}} like cats if you were me?
example.note: The speaker is a mouse.
example.author: Lewis Carroll

gloss: language — to use (a language) — to be expressed with a language

meaning.exp: x_1 is a/the language/dialect used by x_2 to express/communicate x_3 (si'o/du'u, not quote).
meaning.note: For "(of a text) to be written in a language", both x_2 and x_3 are attested, though using x_3 is more common. See quotes.

example.lojban: .i pe'i cizra milxe fa lo nu krici lo du'u lo jugbau cu {{bangu}} le ceizda
example.english: I think it's a little strange to believe that Chinese {{is the language of}} Heaven.
example.speaker: la nalvai

example.lojban: .i ku'i mu'a la'a cu'i so'o da {{co'a se bangu}}
example.english: But, for example, there might be some {{emerging speakers [of the language]}}.
example.author: M. Paul Lewis and Gary F. Simons

example.lojban: .i le dei pagbu cu ro roi {{se bangu la .gliban}}.
example.english: This page is always {{in English}}.
example.note: Example of "(of a text) to be written in a language" expressed with x_2 of {{bangu}}.
example.author: Robin Lee Powell

example.lojban: ni'o da ze'u krici lo du'u lo tai selse'analka'e cukta cu {{te bangu}} fi lo prutce ja darno
example.english: For a long time it was believed that those impenetrable books {{were in}} ancient or distant {{languages}}.
example.note: Example of "(of a text) to be written in a language" expressed with x_3 of {{bangu}}.
example.author: Jorge Luis Borges

example.lojban: .i mi jinvi lo du'u lo me zoi gy jbo.wikipedia.org gy cu bilga co {{te bangu fi lo jbobau}}
example.english: I think stuffs in jbo.wikipedia.org should {{be in Lojban}}.
example.note: Example of "(of a text) to be written in a language" expressed with x_3 of {{bangu}}.
example.speaker: la srasu

gloss: Preposition (tense): retrospective; event already ended

meaning.exp: Retrospective/perfect: signifies that the event has already ended; already.

example.lojban: .i lo jitro be lo te lanme {{ba'o}} cliva lo ra cmana
example.english: The shepherd of the flock {{has already}} left his hill.
example.author: la solpa'i

meaning.exp: in the aftermath of ...; since ...

example.lojban: ni'o {{ba'o}} le krixa ke cladu savru cu co'a klaku fa pi ro le drata prenu
example.english: {{After}} the deafeningly noisy screaming, everyone else started to cry.
example.author: Jin

meaning.exp: is already ended when ...

gloss: Preposition: in language ...

meaning.exp: In language ...; Introduces an unnumbered sumti that plays the role of {{bangu}}'s x<sub>1</sub> in the sentence.
meaning.note: The event described by the bridi is normally an activity associated with language (For example: speaking, writing, reading, making creative works...), in which the sumti introduced with {{bau}} specifies the language being used.

example.lojban: xu do djica lo nu mi cusku fi do {{bau la lojban po'o}}
example.english: Do you want me to speak to you {{in Lojban only}}?
example.author: Robin Lee Powell

example.lojban: .i ku'i .u'adai do kakne lo ka ciska {{bau lo na'e jai se jimpe}}
example.english: However, gain for you that you can write {{in a language that isn't understood [by others]}}.
example.speaker: la janbe

meaning.exp: In (the) language of ...; Introduces an unnumbered sumti that plays the role of {{bangu}}'s x<sub>2</sub> in the sentence.

example.lojban: .i zo'oi Naylte valsi {{sebau}} lo ractu
example.english: "Naylte" is a word {{in the language of}} rabbits.
example.speaker: la nonselcme

example.lojban: mi {{na jai se bau}} zgijbo
example.english: I {{am not a speaker of}} Musical-Lojban.
example.speaker: la gleki

meaning.exp: Expressing ...; Introduces an unnumbered sumti that plays the role of {{bangu}}'s x<sub>3</sub> in the sentence.
meaning.note: Unattested.

gloss: Incorporates sumti into selbri

meaning.exp: Incorporates a sumti into a selbri ({{SELBRI be SUMTI}}). The sumti can be tagged with a FA ({{SELBRI be FA SUMTI}}) or a sumtcita ({{SELBRI be SUMTCITA SUMTI}}) to specify the place it takes in the selbri. If not specified, the sumti takes the x<sub>2</sub> place of the selbri.
meaning.note: Part of the Linkarg construction ({{be TERM (bei TERM)* (be'o)}}), which is attached immediately after a selbri or a tanru-unit. The place structure of a selbri with incorparted sumti isn't defined.

example.lojban: {{claxu be do}} crisa
example.english: Summer {{without you}}
example.note: An example of selbri with incorparted sumti used as a tanru-unit.
example.author: la .cogas.

example.lojban: .i le se cradi .e {{le notci be fo lo tarci}} cu mo
example.english: What about the radio signals? {{The messages to the stars}}?
example.note: An example of the construction {{SELBRI be FA SUMTI}}. In this sentence, the {{lo tarci}} fills the x<sub>4</sub> place of {{notci}} because of the {{fo}}.
example.author: Terry Bisson

example.lojban: .i mi ba prami lo sance {{be}} lo brife {{be bu'u}} lo maxri
example.english: I shall love the sound {{of}} the wind {{in}} the wheat.
example.note: An example of consecutive {{be}} and the construction {{SELBRI be SUMTCITA SUMTI}}. In this sentence, the sumti is parsed as {{lo [sance be lo [brife be bu'u [lo marxi]]]}}, in which {{lo barxi}} fills the {{bu'u}} place of {{brife}}, and {{lo brife be bu'u [lo marxi]}} in turn fills the x<sub>2</sub> place of {{sance}}.
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

gloss: silly, fool — folly, a foolish act

meaning.exp: x_1 is foolish/silly in event/action/property [folly] (ka) x_2; x_1 is a fool.

example.lojban: .i ko co'a xenru {{doi bebna}}
example.english: Start feeling some remorse, {{idiot.}}
example.author: Mèremim

example.lojban: .i ku'i do mi dunli {{lo ka bebna}}
example.english: But you have been just as {{foolish}} as I.
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

example.lojban: .i .o'u no simsa {{se bebna}} pu fasnu
example.english: No similar {{follies}} happened. Phew!
example.speaker: la lunbe

example.lojban: .i le du'u xu kau {{bebna lo ka nerkla}} cu ba se facki ca le nu bevri fi le bartu
example.english: Was {{[she] that dumb, did [she] go in}} or not, we'll see when they carry them out.
example.author: Szymborska Wisława

gloss: to carry, to bring — to be carried — destination — origin, start — route

meaning.exp: x_1 carries/hauls/bears/transports cargo x_2 to x_3 from x_4 over path x_5; x_1 is a carrier/[porter].
meaning.note: The x_2 ~ x_5 of {{bevri}} correspond to the x_1 ~ x_4 of {{klama}}.

example.lojban: .i ko'e carna gi'e troci co {{bevri le cifnu le kumfa kojna noi trixe le toknu}}
example.english: She turned and tried to {{hold the baby over in a corner behind the stove}}.
example.author: Raymond Carver

example.lojban: .i lo me la niuton. tcecmada'u cu junla zbasu sarji gi'e darsi smadi lo du'u lo brabra poi {{bevri lo te gusni fu lo kumfa}} cu bilga lo nu muvdu ja'i lo junla nu muvdu
example.english: The animalcular Newton was a Clockmakerist; and he hazarded the bold guess that the colossus who {{carried a lamp around the room}} would be forced to regulate his movements by clocktime.
example.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

example.lojban: .i ku'i lo bi'unai xrula co'a te tsiju ca lo djedi fi da {{poi se bevri fo lo na te djuno}}
example.english: But one day, a new flower had come up from a seed {{carried from no one knew where}};
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

gloss: to be obliged to ... — (a) must, obligation, duty — (of a standard, custom, etc.) to oblige one to ...

meaning.exp: x_1 is bound/obliged to/has the duty to do/be x_2 in/by standard/agreement x_3; x_1 must do x_2.

example.lojban: .i se ri'a bo sy na {{bilga}} lo nu crino
example.english: Thus, they don't {{need to}} be green.
example.author: Worldbuilding Notes

example.lojban: .i mi gu se ju se nandu gi {{bilga lo ka sanli}}
example.english: I {{must stand}} whether or not it's difficult.
example.note: This sentence is in JACU. To convert it to CLL Lojban, substitute {{gu se ju}} with {{se gu'u}}.
example.author: Djemynai

example.lojban: .i .abu {{bilga}} lo nu korcu kei lo nu marbi lo cnebo lo nu porpi
example.english: She {{had to}} stoop to save her neck from being broken.
example.author: Lewis Carroll

example.lojban: mi'a roroi ckire jecu {{noroi jai te bilga}} jecu gleki lonu do kansa
example.english: (We are) always welcome, {{never obligated}}, glad to have you here.
example.speaker: la ziren
example.note: This sentence is in JACU. To convert it to CLL Lojban, substitute {{jecu}} with {{gi'e}}.

gloss: to become, to change into ... — result of change — condition of change

meaning.exp: x_1 becomes/changes/converts/transforms into x_2 under conditions x_3.

example.lojban: ni'o lo jalge be lo nu ko'a lanli cu zi {{binxo}} lo te lijda be lo jdasi'a
example.english: The queries of the philosopher soon {{became}} doctrines of the church.
example.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

example.lojban: .i va'o lo nu gy djica lo nu polje pa lo tuple zo'u ri pa moi {{lo binxo be lo sirji}}
example.english: If he wanted to bend one of his legs, then that was the first one {{to strech itself out}}.
example.note: "strech itself out" = "become (something) straight"
example.author: Franz Kafka

example.lojban: .i le karce zo'a flecu klama fo le dargu pe le bartu noi {{ca'o manku binxo}}
example.english: Cars slushed by on the street outside, where it {{was getting dark}}.
example.note: An example of a very common tanru formation, where the seltau (modifying part of the tanru) describes the x_2 of the tertau (modified part of the tanru), which is "result of change" here. In this usage, {{manku binxo}} means similar to {{binxo lo manku}}.
example.author: Raymond Carver

example.lojban: .i xy. co'i {{makfa ke marji binxo}}
example.english: They have {{become transmuted}} [instead].
example.note: A counter-example of the above tanru formation pattern. Here, {{marji binxo}} doesn't mean {{binxo lo marji}} "become materialized", but "change in material" instead.
example.author: Worldbuilding Notes

gloss: Grouping: short scope link, strong binding

meaning.exp: Short scope link. Used in various grammatical constructions and acts as a high precedence link, overriding usual left-grouping rules. Chains linked with {{bo}} are grouped to the right. Specific usages are explained below.
Joins tanru units, binding them together closely.

example.lojban: ni'o ze mo'o fenki tcati {{bo}} kansi'u
example.english: VII. The mad tea{{-}}party
example.note: The {{bo}} directly corresponds to the hyphen in the English text. Without the {{bo}} the tanru will group as {{[fenki tcati] kansi'u}}, which roughly translates to "the mad-tea party".
example.author: Lewis Carroll

meaning.exp: Override the default left-grouping in chained connectives. Constituents connected by connectives with {{bo}} are grouped first. Chains linked with {{bo}} are grouped to the right.

example.lojban: .i ku'i mi pu ku tcidu ba'e so'u pagbu be le to'e censa se ciska gi'e ba bo ga'orgau le cukta {{gi'e bo}} co'a bevri
example.english: Yet I had read only the least fragment of that blasphemous rune before closing the book and bringing it away.
example.note: The English sentence is grouped as "I had read... before [closing the book and bringing it away]". If the underlined {{bo}} wasn't there, it'll group as "I had [read... before closing the book] and bringing it away". This example also shows the right-grouping rule with chained {{bo}}: The {{gi'e ba bo}} in the example has a lower priority because it is to the left of the underlined {{gi'e bo}}.
example.author: H. P. Lovecraft

meaning.context: Between a NAhE and a sumti
meaning.exp: Binds NAhE and the sumti together.
meaning.note: Not required in later grammars such as camxes beta or zantufa.

example.lojban: .i mi ka'e binxo lo makcu prenu noi se cinri no {{na'e bo}} lo namcu
example.english: I may become like the grown-ups who are interested in anything nothing {{other than}} figures.
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

meaning.exp: Forms a sentence link along with {{.i}} and the BAI modal. The resulting sentence link ({{.i BAI bo}}) tags the latter bridi as a whole by the BAI modal, and incorporates it to the former (main) bridi. {{BRIDI<sub>1</sub> .i BAI bo BRIDI<sub>2</sub>}} has a similar meaning to {{BRIDI<sub>1</sub> BAI lo su'u BRIDI<sub>2</sub>}} or {{lo su'u BRIDI<sub>2</sub> cu SELBRI lo su'u BRIDI<sub>1</sub>}} (where {{BAI}} is the modal for {{SELBRI}}), but {{.i BAI bo}} also asserts that both the linked bridi are true.

example.lojban: ni'o lo ka jinga nalka'e cu nalvai {{.i mu'i bo}} mi klama be tu mutce bo djica
example.english: It doesn't matter that I can't win, {{because}} I really want to go there.
example.note: The second {{bo}} in this example is of another usage (that inside a tanru).
example.author: Ibuki Tsubasa

meaning.exp: Forms a sentence link along with {{.i}} and the tense. The resulting sentence link ({{.i TENSE bo}}) tags the latter bridi as a whole by the opposite of the tense, and incorporates it to the former (main) bridi. {{BRIDI1 .i TENSE bo BRIDI2}} has a similar meaning to {{BRIDI2 TENSE lo su'u BRIDI1}}, but {{.i TENSE bo}} also asserts that both the linked bridi are true.
meaning.note: The implication of the relationship between connected sentences is the opposite for modals and tenses. The reason is likely historical, as said in Lojban for Beginners (p. 110): "The very astute reader will have noted that ‘afterwards’ should have been {{.i pu bo}}; the analogy with {{ba ku}} won out, though."

example.lojban: .e'u mi'o klama lo korbi {{.i ba bo}} mi do jungau lo lisri be mi
example.english: Let us get to the shore, {{and then}} I'll let you know my story.
example.author: Lewis Carroll

meaning.context: After a connective and a BAI modal
meaning.exp: Binds the connective and the model so that the model signifies the relation between the connected elements. {{.i je BAI bo}} are similar in meaning to {{.i BAI bo}}, and the meanings of other connectives can inferred analogously.
meaning.note: This usage is not unique to {{bo}}. Other grouping words like {{ke}} can also do this, but only those with {{bo}} are attested.

example.lojban: .i ca ro dunra lo clika co'a dunja {{je ja'e bo}} sligu
example.english: Every winter the moss freezes {{and becomes}} solid {{as a result}}.
example.author: Ryan Cross on Science

meaning.context: After a connective and a tense
meaning.exp: Binds the connective and the tense so that the tense signifies the time relation between the connected elements. {{.i je TENSE bo}} are similar in meaning to {{.i TENSE bo}}, and the meanings of other connectives can inferred analogously.
meaning.note: This usage is not unique to {{bo}}. Other grouping words like {{ke}} can also do this, but only those with {{bo}} are attested.

example.lojban: .i loi sorska cinta ko fi ko'a cu se punji {{.i je ba bo}} loi xekri tabno ko'a gacri
example.english: Paint it with colorful pigments, {{and soon enough}} it'll be covered in black charcoal.
example.author: Noise and Bells

meaning.exp: Forms a sentence link along with {{.i}}. The resulting sentence link is formally the same as {{.i}}, but is used to indicate the two sentences linked are closely related.
meaning.note: In this usage, like a semicolon in English. This usage is not described in CLL or BPFK, but is compatible with them. See also {{.e}} in ajbo.

meaning.exp: Forms a sentence link along with {{.i}}. The resulting sentence link separates bridi, but doesn't reset bridi level. Multiple bridi separated with {{.i bo}} shares the same prenex.
meaning.note: Not compatible with the previous usage.

gloss: Letteral: convert word to letteral

meaning.exp: Combines with the previous word to make a Lojban letteral. The resulting lettral, if not made from a letteral (see the next meaning) and used alone, refers to the last sumti starting with the word.
meaning.note: The following words cannot be convert into letteral with {{bu}}: {{bu}}, {{fa'o}}, {{zei}}, any cmavo in BAhE, erasure words ({{si}}, {{sa}}, {{su}}), quotation starters ({{lu}}, {{lo'u}} and any cmavo in ZOI).

example.lojban: .i ta'i ma pilno zo bo {{lonu jufra lasna}} .i {{nubu}} cu cizra makfa zo'o
example.english: How [do I] use {bo} {{to bind sentences together}}? {{It}} is black magic haha
example.note: When determining the referent of a letteral pro-sumti, the gadri ({{lo}}, {{le}}, {{la}}) of a description sumti is ignored. In this utterance, {{nubu}} refers to {{lonu jufra lasna}}, as the description {{nu jufra lasna}} starts with the word {{nu}}.
example.speaker: la melmi

example.lojban: .i lo glico panra be {{lu catni lojbo li'u}} se smuni lo du'u {{la'e lu bu lu'u}} po'o jetnu je drani je mulno lojbo noi fau lo nu masno farvi ku jai to'e sai lakne fai lo ka jetnu
example.english: The English equivalent of {{"Official Lojban"}} mostly implies that {{it}} is the only right, correct and  omplete Lojban, which, given the lack of progress over the last years, is a very improbable case.
example.note: {{lu bu}} refers to {{lu catni lojbo li'u}}, which is the last sumti started with {{lu}}. {{la'e lu bu lu'u}} means "what {{lu catni lojbo li'u}} refers to", thus, the Lojban that is said to be "official".
example.author: la uakci

meaning.exp: Convert a letteral to another (related) letteral.
meaning.note: The ones defined in the CLL are {{.y'y. bu }} for {{h}}, {{ky. bu}} for {{q}}, {{vy. bu}} for {{w}}, {{ty. bu}} for {{þ}} (thorn) and {{dy. bu}} for {{ð}} (eth).

example.lojban: ni'o la tokpono cu pilno so zunsna to jy. .e ky. .e ly. .e my. .e py. .e sy. .e ty. .e {{vy. bu}} toi .e mu karsna to .a bu .e .e bu .e .i bu .e .o bu .e .u bu toi
example.english: Toki Pona uses nine consonants (j k l m n p s t {{w}}) and five vowels (a e i o u).
example.author: Blinry

gloss: Attitudial (intensity indicator): extremely intense attitude

meaning.exp: Intensity Indicator. Used to express an extremely intense attitude. When following an indicator or vocative, it expresses that this attitude is extremely intense.
meaning.note: Generally reserved for expressing an uncontrollably strong or the strongest attitude one could ever have, though some dispute this reservation. The following two examples are examples of extremely strong attitudes, where {{cai}} applies even under the reservation.

example.lojban: .i ja'e bo mi pu'o lifri fe lo vajrai pe lo mi nunji'e .i fasnu fa {{.u'a cai}}
example.english: Thus, I was about to experience the most important thing of my life, What happened was... {{OMFG (literally: "feeling of extreme gain")}}
example.author: Djemynai

example.lojban:
.i lo'u zo gusta zo'u xu genai gusta da lo vitke gi gusta lo vitke da .i ja'o se smuni .y l l l lo nu m m mi'o ... le'u
.i co'a gatagatat desku ke bacru nandu
.i lo'u ... .y m m m mi'o ... {{.iicaiii}} le'u
example.english:
"And 'restaurant' doesn't mean a place for serving food, but a place cooking people and serving them. And that m-m-means that w-w-we ..."
He began to shake and tremble, and tremble and shake, so that he couldn't go on.
"They w-w-we ... {{Oh dear!}}"
example.note: This example uses CBM, where {{gatagatat}} functions as a brivla.
example.author: Kenji Miyazawa

gloss: to vanish, to disappear — location of disappearance — to stop sensing/detecting x<sub>1</sub> at ...

meaning.exp: x_1 vanishes/disappears from location x_2; x_1 ceases to be observed at x_2 using senses/sensor x_3.
meaning.note: I didn't find usage of {{canci}}'s x_3.

example.lojban: .i mi pinfu le mi purci pu le nu ri {{canci mo'u ku}}
example.english: I am a captor of the past until it {{fades into the dark}}
example.author: la xrula

example.lojban: ni'o je'u ka'u lo solri ca lo nu dormidju fi lo mergu'e cu {{canci lo fasygu'e}}
example.english: Everybody knows that when it is noon in the United States the sun {{is setting over France}}.
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

gloss: Preposition (tense): continuative/progressive; event ongoing/in progress

meaning.exp: Continuative/Progressive: signifies that the event is ongoing.

example.lojban: .i do ca lo nu do mrobi'o cu {{ca'o klama lo do zdani}}
example.english: You {{were on your way home}} when you died.
example.author: Andy Weir

meaning.exp: while ... is ongoing; during ...
meaning.note: The sumti introduced by {{ca'o}} indicates an ongoing event that encompasses the situation.

example.lojban: ni'o ca pa nicte ku {{ca'o lo nu ly. sipna kei}} lo nanmu makcu noi cpana lo ranmi fagri cipni ku'o cu tolcanci
example.english: One night {{as he slept}}, an old man appeared on a phoenix.
example.author: Demi

meaning.exp: (event is) ongoing when ...
meaning.note: The sumti introduced by {{ca'o}} indicates an event encompassed by the ongoing situation. It does not give the duration of the main event ({{ZEhA}}s do that), it only indicates that the main event completely overlaps another event.

example.lojban: .i la .gregor. {{ca'o lo nu lo ckiku cu carna}} cu dansu sruri lo stela
example.english: {{As the key turned round}}, Gregor was turning around the lock [with it].
example.author: Franz Kafka

gloss: (of a group) to discuss, to talk about ... — topic, subject of discussion

meaning.exp: x_1(s) (mass normally, but 1 individual/jo'u possible) discuss(es)/talk(s) about topic/subject x_2.
meaning.note: x_1 need not be the complete group participating in the discussion. When x_1 is one individual, it can be taken as "x_1 participates in discussion about x_2".

example.lojban: .i li'a sai ba'e mi na {{casnu}} lo simsa
example.english: Clearly I would not {{talk on}} such a subject!
example.author: Lewis Carroll

example.lojban: .i ba zi ku lo junla mi'u sai noi suksa muvdu gi'e toldikni dikni cu binxo {{lo se casnu be lo xalbo}}
example.english: ..., and soon the clock itself, with its falling movements and irregular regularity, became {{a theme for jesters}}.
example.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

example.lojban: .i mabla tepi'o lonu {{casnu}} lo na lojbo bau la jbobau
example.english: It's bad for {{talking about}} something not Lojban-related in Lojban.
example.speaker: la srasu

gloss: to look at, to watch, to gaze at — to be looked at, to be watched

meaning.exp: x_1 looks at/examines/views/inspects/regards/watches/gazes at x_2.

example.lojban: .i mutce jundi {{catlu}} ro da noi {{pu se catlu}}
example.english: They very carefully {{looked}} everywhere that {{was looked at before}}.
example.author: la lalxu

example.lojban: .i ku'i nau ku cyny. co'a terpa gi je simxu {{catlu}} lo vo'a flira noi ba'o mutce co se gacri lo kruji
example.english: But now, the two became freightened, and {{looked at}} each other's cream-covered face.
example.note: This example uses a variant connective system. To convert it into CLL/BPFK Lojban, replace {{gi je}} with {{gi'e}}.
example.author: Kenji Miyazawa

example.lojban: .i lo penmi be mi jo'u {{lo se catlu be mi}} cu ju'o cliva ba'i lo drata poi ba penmi ja catlu
example.english: The people I meet now, {{the things I'm seeing now}}, they'll surely leave and replaced by what's ahead of me.
example.author: doriko

gloss: to kill, to murder — to be killed — method of killing

meaning.exp: x_1 (agent) kills/slaughters/murders x_2 by action/method x_3.

example.lojban: ni'o {{lo catra be le nanmu goi ko'a}} cu du mi
example.english: {{The killer of the man (called "ko'a" from now on)}} is me.
example.author: Ryūnosuke Akutagawa

example.lojban: .i lo marde cu {{catra}} lo ma'a ka pacna kei ca lo za'i lo ma'a balvi cu se lebna
example.english: Morals {{killed}} our hopes while our futures continue to be taken from us
example.author: Neru

example.lojban: .i lu ca ku ai sei ny cusku mi platu lo prane {{te catra}} li'u
example.english: "Now," she said, "I'll devise the perfect {{plan to put an end [to her]}}!"
example.author: Brothers Grimm

gloss: expert, competent in ..., skilled at ... — expertise, profession, skill — standard of skill

meaning.exp: x_1 is an expert/pro/has prowess in/is skilled at x_2 (event/activity) by standard x_3.

example.lojban: .i li'a mi na {{certu}} lo ka sanga
example.english: Obviously I'm not {{good at}} singing.
example.author: Djemynai

example.lojban: .i my se cau nai lo nu jerna cu ba'o binxo lo simlu {{be lo ka certu be ro cuntu poi srana la .gregor. bei lo rirni}}
example.english: She had become used to the idea, not without reason, {{that she is an expert to his parents about the things that concerned Gregor}}.
example.note: The only usage I can find for {{certu}}'s x<sub>3</sub>.
example.author: Franz Kafka

example.lojban: .oi sai la'a lo nu frili ke cikna binxo cu vajni ke renvi {{se certu}} lo blupinxe
example.english: Oww! Waking up easily is probably an important survival {{skill}} of a vampire.
example.author: Robin Lee Powell

gloss: to learn, learner — to be learned, facts learned — subject of learning — source of learning — learning method

meaning.exp: x_1 learns x_2 (du'u) about subject x_3 from source x_4 (obj./event) by method x_5 (event/process).

example.lojban: .i mi {{cilre lo du'u ta'i ma kau zgipli lo flani kei}} mu'i lonu zdile
example.english: I'm {{learning how to play a flute}} for fun.
example.speaker: la ziren

example.lojban: .i mi ra'a {{cilre}} so'i da fo la lunbe ku noi .uinai cando do'e le jbogu'e ca

example.lojban: .i mu'i ku so'i da pilno {{lo laldo ve cilre}} lo ka {{cilre fi lo catni lojbo}}

example.author: la uakci

example.english: Which means (entails) that [you] can {{learn by making Pokémon names}}.
example.speaker: la nonselcme

meaning.exp: x_1 (abstraction) interests/is interesting to x_2; x_2 is interested in x_1.

example.lojban:
— .i xu do viska lo cnino trene
— .i go'i lo pixra be lo 777moi klesi trene .i ri na {{jai cinri}} mi
example.english:
— Did you see the new train?
— Yep, saw the picture of the Class 777. It didn't {{interest}} me.
example.speaker: latkerlo, la samflir

example.lojban: xu nai lo zekri poi .i'y gasnu ke'a cu {{cinri}} do
example.english: Doesn't the crime it ( = the word ie'o) caused {{interest}} you?
example.speaker: la lunbe
example.note: {{.i'y}} is a proposed cmavo equivalent to {{.i bu}}. Note that this example doesn't need {{jai}} because the x_1 of {{zekri}} is already an event.

example.lojban: .i lo nu citka cu cizra {{cinri}} sy.

example.author: Robin Lee Powell

example.lojban: .i mi ka'e binxo lo makcu prenu noi {{se cinri}} no na'e bo lo namcu

example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

meaning.exp: x_1 inscribes/writes x_2 on display/storage medium x_3 with writing implement x_4; x_1 is a scribe.
meaning.noshownote: x_4 is sometimes seen to mean "writing medium", probably due to influence from {{vreji}} or {{cusku}}.

example.lojban: do {{ciska}} fi lo mi risna fe lu ai mi do no roi cliva li'u
example.english: You {{wrote}} on my heart the phrase "I'm never going to leave you".

example.lojban: la .dorotis. cu catlu lo nenri be la solji mapku gi'e viska lo so'u valsi poi {{se ciska fi lo nenri korbi}}

example.lojban: .i mi ca mabla za'a {{ciska fo}} lo batkyfoi

meaning.exp: x_1 eats/ingests/consumes (transitive verb) x_2.

example.author: la lalxu

example.lojban: {{lo se citka ku}} mo

example.author: la lalxu

meaning.exp: x_1 is strange/weird/deviant/bizarre/odd to x_2 in property x_3 (ka).

example.lojban: .i ku'i ro da {{cizra}} ca lo cabdei
example.english: But everything {{is strange}} today.
example.author: Lewis Carroll

example.lojban: .i a'o {{na cizra}} do fa tu'a ti
example.english: I hope (something about) this {{is not strange}} to you.
example.author: la solpa'i

example.lojban: .i la gregor cu {{se cizra}} lo vrici sance be lo nu citka

example.author: Franz Kafka

meaning.exp: x_1 leaves/goes away/departs/parts/separates from x_2 via route x_3.

example.lojban: .i .e'a ko mi {{cliva}}
example.english: Go ahead and {{leave}} me
example.author: Jonathan Coulton

example.lojban: .i ri'a tu'a lo ckule cidja mi binxo co bilma lo za'i ru'i {{se cliva lo ciblu lo kanla}}
example.english: Because of the school's food, I became sick, with {{blood}} continuously {{goes out through my eyes}}.
example.author: la blutolpinxe

example.lojban: ni'o xu lo prenu co vajni cu ge'i ca ranji lo nu kansa ku gi ve'u sepli do gi'e {{pu co'a cliva fi lo drata se litru}}
example.english: As for the people important [to you], do they continue to accompany you? Or are they now distant and separated from you, {{having departed via their own paths}}?
example.author: doriko

gloss: small — aspect/property/dimension of smallness — standard of smallness

meaning.exp: x_1 is small in property/dimension(s) x_2 (ka) as compared with standard/norm x_3.
meaning.note: Despite the "dimension" in its definition's x<sub>2</sub>, the meaning of {{cmalu}} extends to "something small in amount/number; a small number; a small amount of ...", and sentences like {{mi djuno lo cmalu lo jbobau}} are considered idiomatic by some fluent Lojbanists.

example.lojban: .i le zdani ku {{cmalu}}
example.english: Their house {{was small}}.
example.author: la lalxu

example.lojban: .i ku'i le voksa be la ractu cu {{cmalu}}
example.english: but Rabbit's voice {{was tiny}}…
example.author: la lalxu

example.lojban: .i ku'i lo te frica cu {{cmalu}}

example.lojban: mi dejni {{lo cmalu be lo jdini}} ru vau doi la din .i xu ru cusku fi do
example.english: I owe {{a little money}} to him, Din. Did he tell you?
example.author: William Gibson

example.lojban: .i la silnytca zo'u silna .i tcadu je'u .i ku'i {{cmalu cmalu fi tu'a lo bratca}}
example.english: As for Salt [Lake] City: salt. It's really a city, but it's {{small small by large city standards}}.
example.speaker: la janbe

meaning.exp: x_1 is a structure word of grammatical class x_2, with meaning/function x_3 in usage (language) x_4.

example.lojban: ni'o {{zoi ty. e .ty cmavo fi lo du'u lo lifri}} cu sepli le drata pagbu be le jufra
example.english: {{The particle e, which [introduces] a direct object}}, separates it from the rest of the sentence.

example.lojban: .i xu la .lucil. cu jinvi le du'u lo nu jimpe cu se filri'a lo nu pilno {{lo cmavo be le cmavrfa}} tu'a lo no sumti jonai lo ro sumti
example.english: Does Lucilla thinks understanding is made easy when either none or all of the sumti is [tagged] with {{FA (cmavo of class FA)}}?
example.speaker: la varik
example.note: This sentence is in JACU. To convert it to CLL Lojban, substitute {{jonai}} with {{.onai}}. Also, {{cmavrfa}} is a type-3 zi'evla. {{cmavrfa}} = cmav-r-FA.

example.lojban: .icaku mi djica tu'a {{lo cmavo be ma'oi ca'a bei tu'a zo je'u}}
example.english: Now I want {{a CAhA (cmavo of class CAhA) that means similarly to je'u}}.
example.speaker: la srasu

example.lojban: .i so'ida .oiru'e {{temci cmavo fo lo jbobau}}
example.english: There are so many {{tense particles in Lojban...}}
example.speaker: la melmi

gloss: name, title — to be called as ..., to be named — to name, to call ... as ...

meaning.exp: x_1 (quoted word(s)) is a/the name/title/tag of x_2 to/used-by namer/name-user x_3 (person).

example.lojban: .i ma {{cmene}} do poi ke'a na slabu mi
example.english: What {{is}} your {{name}}, unfamiliar one?
example.author: 40mP

example.lojban: ni'o lo jmive poi ka'e prami cu ca ca'o {{se cmene}} fi lo remna fa zo remna
example.english: A living thing that can love is now {{being called}} "human" by mankind.
example.author: niki

example.lojban: .i ki'u ma lo cmalu ninmu cu {{te cmene}} dy lu te makfa li'u
example.english: Why did the little woman {{call}} her (Dorothy) "a sorceress"?
example.author: L. Frank Baum

gloss: novelty, unfamiliar — to be unfamiliar with ...

meaning.exp: x_1 is new/unfamiliar/novel to observer x_2 in feature x_3 (ka) by standard x_4; x_1 is a novelty.
meaning.note: I only found usages of x<sub>1</sub> and x<sub>2</sub> places.
meaning.noshownote: I found one usage of the x_3 place, but sadly the sentence has bracketing issues and I couldn't make sense of the sentence.

example.lojban: .i zgadi fa lo nu cusku fi do fe lo du'u lo xrani mi {{na cnino}}
example.english: I really should tell you that the world's dangers {{are nothing new}} to me.
example.author: Noise and Bells (la janbe)

meaning.exp: Initiative: signifies that the event starts.

example.lojban: .i mi {{co'a}} na kakne lo nu jitro
example.english: I {{start to}} be unable to control.
example.author: Fyren

meaning.exp: at the starting point of ...
starts when ...; since ...; from ...

example.lojban: .i xy. to'e lazni gunka {{co'a lo cerni}} co'u lo nicte gi'e na djuno lo du'u lo si'o gleki cu mo kau
example.english: He worked hard {{from morning}} till night and did not know what joy was.
example.author: L. Frank Baum

gloss: Preposition (tense): cessative; event stops

meaning.exp: Cessative: signifies that the event ends. The event is not neccesarily completed.

example.lojban: .i ko {{co'u}} tolckire gi'e prami mi
example.english: {{Stop being}} thankless and love me.
example.author: José María Lacalle García

meaning.exp: at the ending point of ... (even if not done)

example.lojban: .i {{co'u}} lo nu terxra kei ly ganse lo nu le mirli co'a jmive
example.english: {{As}} he {{finished}} painting, he felt that the deer came to life.
example.author: Demi

meaning.exp: ends when ...; until ...

example.lojban: .i sa'u ko troci {{co'u}} lo nu claxu lo titnanba
example.english: You just keep on trying {{till}} you run out of cake.
example.author: Jonathan Coulton

gloss: upon, to be on ... — location on which x<sub>1</sub> lies, location of x<sub>1</sub>

meaning.exp: x_1 is upon/atop/resting on/lying on [the upper surface of] x_2 in frame of reference/gravity x_3.

example.lojban: ni'o lo botpi cu {{cpana}} lo jubme bu'u lo midju be lo kumfa
example.english: The caraffe {{stood on}} a table in the midst of the room.
example.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

example.lojban: .i ba ku ko'e zgana le pixra be le cifnu be'o {{poi cpana le ckana ku'o}} .i je lebna le se go'i
example.english: Then she noticed the baby's picture {{on the bed}} and picked it up.
example.author: Raymond Carver

example.lojban: .i lo re moi cu cusku lu ma pu citka {{pi lo cpana be lo mi palta}} li'u
example.english: The second said, "Who has been eating {{off my plate}}?"
example.note: Literally "... eating some of that is on my plate?"
example.author: Brothers Grimm

gloss: Seperator: seperates leading sumti from main selbri

meaning.exp: Elidable marker: separates selbri from preceding sumti, allows preceding terminator elision.
meaning.note: As defined in CLL and BPFK Lojban. {{cu}} is elidable when there are no terminators needed in place of {{cu}}. When elidable, {{cu}} is usually elided when only pro-sumti precede it; when the preceding sumti is more complex (for example, {{la'e di'u}} or quotes), {{cu}} is sometimes kept to keep the sentence structure clear.

example.lojban: .i lo pixra {{cu}} mapti
example.english: One drawing goes along all right.
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

example.lojban: .i do lo nu djuno lo du'u ma kau smuvanbi {{cu}} nitcu lo nu jdice lo du'u ma kau smuni
example.english: You'll [often] need to know the context to decide what things mean.
example.note: An example of {{cu}} closing off multiple subordinate clauses ({{lo nu djuno ...}} and {{lo du'u ma kau smuvanbi}}) at once. In this sentence, the full terminator sequence in place of {{cu}} would be {{vau kei ku vau kei ku}}. Also note that there can be a {{cu}} in {{ma kau (cu) smuvanbi}}, but it's elided: as there aren't terminators needed in the first place, using {{cu}} here offers no real benefit.
example.author: Blinry

example.lojban: .i se cau le cartu poi dunda ke'a mi {{cu}} bajra litru se ka'a le balvi poi mi cuxna ku
example.english: So without the map that was given to me, [I'll] run towards the future that I've chosen myself.
example.note: An example of elidable {{cu}} kept for clarity. The last {{ku}} in this sentence is kept for metrical purpose.
example.author: Last Note.

meaning.exp: Starts a bridi tail (main selbri + trailing sumti if any). Termintate with {{vau}}.
meaning.note: This sense is compatible with the above sense, and also enables {{cu}} to appear when there are no preceding sumti. This sense of {{cu}} is the basis of JACU and is supported by camxes beta, camxes experimental and zantufa.

example.lojban: .i sei fa'a ti'a catlu {{cu}} zvati fa pa nobli je ro'opno simlu zdani
example.english: They looked back. There they saw a single, elegant Western-style home.
example.note: As a {{sei}}-structure isn't a sumti, there are no sumti before {{cu}}, so this sentence doesn't parse in CLL/BPFK Lojban. In CLL/BPFK Lojban, {{se'u}} must be used in place of {{cu}} here to close off the {{sei}}-structure properly.
example.author: Kenji Miyazawa

example.lojban: .i mi dansu je {{cu}} kansa la terdi lo ka carna
example.english: I dance and spin with the Earth.
example.note: An example of JACU. In this sentence, {{je}} connects two bridi-tails, {{dansu}} and {{cu kansa ...}}. Replace {{je cu}} with {{gi'e}} to convert it to CLL/BPFK Lojban.
example.author: Djemynai

gloss: to express, to say — expression — audience — communication format

meaning.exp: x_1 (agent) expresses/says x_2 (sedu'u/text/lu'e concept) for audience x_3 via expressive medium x_4.

example.lojban: ni'o le ractu ku {{cusku}} lu xu do djica lo nu citka li'u

example.lojban: .i ka'e {{cusku}} zo co'o fi ro da

example.lojban: .i my. {{cusku}} lo se du'u my. manci catlu po'o lo mi melbi lerfu
example.english: She (my mother) said she was just marvelling at my beautiful handwriting.

example.lojban: .i lo zbasu noi {{manku cusku fo lo drata se zbasu}} cu simlu lo ka bacru lo jetnu voksa se pi'o lo junla
example.english: The creator, who {{spoke obscurely in his other works}}, seemed to utter an authentic voice with the clock;
example.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

gloss: object, thing

meaning.exp: x_1 is a material object enduring in space-time; x_1 is a thing.

example.lojban: .i {{lo va dacti}} cu mo
example.english: What is {{that object}}?
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

example.lojban: .i mi'a ba zi catra le jitro be {{le dacti}}
example.english: We will soon kill the controller of {{the thing}}.

example.lojban: .i le nu mi ba ba'o {{dacti}} zo'u sruri fa lo tarci

example.author: Noise and Bells (la janbe)

gloss: Preposition (tense): pausative; event temporarily suspended

example.lojban: la .bil. uu pu {{de'a}} ciska fi lo tanbo lo degji

gloss: Voicative: identifies the listener ("you")

meaning.exp: Generic vocative marker; identifies intended listener/audience. When followed by a sumti, the sumti is the intended listener/audience. When followed by a cmevla, it is understood as {{doi la CMEVLA}}. When followed by a selbri, it is understood as {{doi le SELBRI}}. {{doi}} opens a vocative phrase, which automatically closes when the sumti or selbri after {{doi}} is completed. The vocative phrase can also be closed explicitly with {{do'u}}.

example.lojban: ni'o {{doi mi poi mo'u verba}} .i pau ma poi prenu cu se prami
example.english: {{To me when completing childhood}}, who do [you] love now?
example.author: doriko

example.lojban: .i {{doi dirba}} o'u dai ko sursipna iu cai
example.english: {{Darling,}} (I feel you are relaxed), have a restful sleep <3
example.note: An example of {{doi SELBRI}}.
example.author: la fagri

example.lojban: .i {{doi .dinas. noi dirba mi do'u}} .au do mi kansa lo nu vi cnita
example.english: {{Dinah, my dear!}} I wish you were down here with me!
example.note: An example of {{doi}} followed by a cmevla. A cmevla inside a vocative phrase can take a relative clause/phrase, and is taken as the same as {{doi la CMEVLA <relative phrase/clause>}}.
example.author: Lewis Carroll

gloss: Elidable Terminator: terminates vocative phrase

meaning.exp: Ends vocative phrase, which is started with {{DOI}} or {{COI}}. Elidable.
meaning.note: For demonstration purposes, the example sentences here only shows {{do'u}} in unelidable position. See the words in selma'o {{DOI}} and {{COI}} to see elided {{do'u}}.

example.lojban: .i {{ju'i vitke do'u}} sutra klama .e'o
example.english: {{Hey [visitors]!}} Come here quickly!
example.note: If the {{do'u}} was elided in this sentence, the {{vitke}} would run into the {{sutra klama}} behind and form a tanru.
example.noshownote: Original has {{vitka}}, which I presume is a typo of {{vitke}}.
example.author: Kenji Miyazawa

example.lojban: .i .o'u {{nu'e do'u}} mi'o mo'u sepli simxu
example.english: Don't worry — {{I promise}}, we'll be together again.
example.note: If the {{do'u}} was elided in this sentence, the {{nu'e}} would take {{mi'o}} as a component of the vocative phrase, making {{mi'o}} the intended listener instead of the x<sub>1</sub> of the main selbri.
example.author: Noise and Bells (la janbe)

example.lojban: .i {{doi .dinas. noi dirba mi do'u}} .au do mi kansa lo nu vi cnita
example.english: {{Dinah, my dear!}} I wish you were down here with me!
example.note: If the {{do'u}} was elided in this sentence, the vocative phrase would close right before the {{kansa}}.
example.author: Lewis Carroll

meaning.exp: Equality/identity predicate. x_1 equals x_2, x_3, etc. It expresses that multiple different sumti actually refer to the same thing.

example.lojban: ni'o lo catra be le nanmu goi ko'a cu {{du}} mi
example.english: The killer of the man (called "ko'a" from now on) {{is}} me.

meaning.exp: Substitution for {{du'u}}.

gloss: Connective: sumti afterthought and

meaning.exp: Logical connective: sumti afterthought and. Connects two sumti, such that the containing bridi is true if and only if it is true for each of the connected sumti.
meaning.note: Supplanted with {{je}} in JACU.

example.lojban: .i po'o do {{.e}} mi zvati
example.english: Just you {{and}} me [are here].
example.author: Andy Weir

example.lojban: .i .ei mi pajni ji'u lo se zukte {{.e nai}} lo valsi
example.english: I ought to have judged by deeds {{and not}} by words.
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

meaning.exp: Letteral for e. When used alone, refers to the most recent sumti starting with {{e}}.

example.lojban: ni'o {{la .em.}} ca lo nu klama ti te zu'e lo nu bu'u xabju cu citno je melbi speni .i lo solri jo'u lo brife cu cnegau {{.e bu}} ji'a
example.english: When {{Aunt Em}} came there to live she was a young, pretty wife. The sun and wind had changed {{her}} (= Aunt Em), too.
example.author: L. Frank Baum

meaning.exp: Equivalent to {{.i ji'a}}. Starts a sentence that is a direct continuation of the last sentence. Sentences separated with {{.e}} are considered to refer to the same event/concept, and are only seperated becuase of grammatical reasons.
meaning.note: Adopting ajbo prerequires adopting JACU. {{.e nai}} is neither defined or used.

example.lojban: ni'o ca le prula'i mi tolcirko lo tutci pe po skami xrazba {{.e}} mi finti le'i tolmulno pixra be lo skapypre .i ai ba di'a gunka tu'a ti
example.english: (New topic) Last [time] I recovered my digital painting tools {{and}} I made this unfinished drawing of a skinwalker. I intend to keep working on this. <picture>
example.speaker: la srasu
example.note:
This utterance is in a divergent variety that has many differences with the baseline grammar:
  • {{po}} is used as in jboponei, where it converts a bridi directly to a sumti, and corresponds to {{lo su'u}} in baseline.
  • {{.e}} is used as in ajbo, where it continues the same concept with another sentence, and corresponds to {{.i ji'a}} in baseline.
  • {{le'i}} is used as in gadganzu, where it functions as a demonstrative article (think of it as pointing to the <picture>), and corresponds to {{ti noi ... (ku'o)}} in baseline.
This utterance serves as an example of the modularity of Lojban variaties, as said three differences from the baseline are unrelated to each other and can be employed independently.

gloss: Place Structure: tag original x<sub>1</sub> swapped out by jai

meaning.exp: Sumti place tag: tag a sumti moved out of numbered place structure by {{jai}}.
meaning.note: The meaning of {{fai}} without {{jai}} is undefined. BPFK claims {{fai}} has a rafsi form {{-fax-}}, but the rafsi is taken by {{fraxu}}.

example.lojban: .i ba zi bo .abu {{jai suksa fai}} lo nu pejgau lo xance gi'e jgari lo vacri

example.author: Mèremim

gloss: to translate, translator — to be translated, original text — target language — source language — (a work of) translation

meaning.exp: x_1 translates text/utterance x_2 to language x_3 from language x_4 with translation result x_5.

example.lojban: .i .e'u nai cai la nicte cadzu ba mulno spogau lo se terpa {{da poi fanva dei lo na logji bangu}}

example.note: Those who are keen on quantification will notice that this sentence uses existential quantification on {{da poi ...}}, which means if there are multiple translators, only "at least one of them" will be destroyed, instead of "all" which is suggested by the content of the text. (Such interpretation would be accomplished with universal quantification {{ro da poi ...}}). Actually, the {{da}} is being used here as a generic pronoun, which is a common usage in texts from the 2000s.

meaning.exp: x_1 develops/evolves towards/into x_2 from x_3 through stages x_4.

meaning.exp: Converts the following time tag into its space equivalent. The following time tag must be one of {{ZAhO}}, {{TAhE}} or {{number + ROI}}.

gloss: Preposition: created by...

meaning.exp: Created by ...; Introduces an unnumbered sumti that plays the role of {{finti}}'s x<sub>1</sub> in the sentence.
meaning.note: The event described by the bridi is normally associated with the creation of something, and that the creator is the referent of the tagged sumti. Often seen in titles to indicate the author of a text.

example.lojban: ki'e {{jai fi'e}} mupli
example.english: Thanks, example-{{creator}}!
example.speaker: la fagri

example.lojban: clani kerlo {{fi'e}} la fagri

example.author: la fagri

example.lojban: .i mi jinvi lo du'u so'i cnino zmadu zgike {{be fi'e mi}} cu zabna
example.english: I think many newer songs {{by me}} are nice.

example.lojban: .i gidva ro da fa lo se platu {{be fi'e mi}}

meaning.exp: Creating work ...; Introduces an unnumbered sumti that plays the role of {{finti}}'s x<sub>2</sub> in the sentence.

meaning.exp: Creating with purpose ...; Introduces an unnumbered sumti that plays the role of {{finti}}'s x<sub>3</sub> in the sentence.

meaning.exp: Creating from ...; Introduces an unnumbered sumti that plays the role of {{finti}}'s x<sub>4</sub> in the sentence.

example.lojban: lo du'u nandu fa lo nu cusku lu'e lo smuni poi simsa zo javni ku'o {{vefi'e}} lo drata smuni cu nibli pe'i lo du'u le javni smuni cu xamgu zmadu

meaning.exp: Converts the following selbri into a modal/tag/preposition. The resulting preposition introduces an unnumbered sumti that plays the role of the converted selbri's x<sub>1</sub> in the sentence.
meaning.note: The exact relation between the introduced sumti and the rest of the sentence has not been rigorously defined and is usually understood in an ad-hoc manner. The same goes for BAI prepositions.

example.lojban: .i do prane ro zu'i {{fi'o morji le do panzi}}
