example.speaker: la nalvai

example.lojban: ni'o lo cmalu noltru cu {{mutce frica}} lo makcu prenu lo ka ma kau sidbo lo se junri ce'u
example.english: The little prince {{was very different from}} those of the grown-ups on which ideas were matters of consequence.
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

example.lojban: .i ku'i {{lo te frica}} cu cmalu
example.english: But {{the discrepancy}} was small.
example.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

gloss: lid, (of an object) to cover — to be covered

meaning.exp: x_1 is a cover/[lid/top] for covering/concealing/sheltering x_2.

example.lojban: .i loi sorska cinta ko fi ko'a cu se punji .i je ba bo loi xekri tabno ko'a {{gacri}}
example.english: Paint it with colorful pigments, and soon enough black charcoal {{will cover}} it.
example.author: Noise and Bells

example.lojban: .i pluka fa lo nu {{lo clika cu gacri}} lo loldi be lo ricfoi tai lo matci
example.english: It's [always] nice to {{have moss covering}} the forest floor like a carpet...
example.author: Worldbuilding Notes

example.lojban: .i ba za lo na'e clani la snime blabi cu kargau lo kanla gi'e lafti {{lo gacri be lo mrovau}} gi'e tsebi'o gi'e di'a jmive
example.english: In a short time Snow White opened her eyes, lifted {{the lid of the coffin}}, sat up and came back to life again.
example.author: Brothers Grimm

gloss: to do, to bring about, (of a person, object) to cause — effect

meaning.exp: x_1 [person/agent] is an agentive cause of event x_2; x_1 does/brings about x_2.
meaning.note: Despite the "[person/agent]" in the definition, the x<sub>1</sub> needs not be volitional (which distinguishes it from {{zukte}}), nor does it need to be animate. The x<sub>1</sub> is normally not an event, as the case of x<sub>1</sub> being an event is covered by {{rinka}}.

example.lojban: .i .io la cevni zo'u doi lo zvati be vi ti ko {{gasnu}} lo nu sance fa lo gleki si'azgi
example.english: To God on high, all you in this place, {{let}} hymns ring out in joyful chorus!
example.author: Noise and Bells (la janbe)

example.lojban: .i mulgau lo co'a {{se gasnu}}
example.english: ..., [and] complete what [we have] started {{to do}}.
example.author: Djemynai

example.lojban: xu nai lo zekri {{poi .i'y gasnu ke'a}} cu cinri do
example.english: Doesn't the crime {{it ( = the word ie'o) caused}} interest you?
example.speaker: la lunbe
example.note: {{.i'y}} is a proposed cmavo equivalent to {{.i bu}}.

example.lojban: mi nelci lo'e gundi jibri .i ku'i ri {{tatpi gasnu}}
example.english: I like industrial jobs. But they {{are tiring}}.
example.note: This sentence showcase a common phenomenon of putting the effect in the seltau position of {{gasnu}}. In this sentence, {{tatpi gasnu}} is similar in meaning to {{gasnu lo nu tatpi}}. In such tanru formation, the x<sub>2</sub> of {{gasnu}} is usually left unfilled, and is assumed to be {{lo nu <seltau>}}.
example.speaker: qimar

gloss: Connective: forethought connective question

meaning.exp: Logical connective: all but tanru-internal forethought connective question. Asks the listener to supply a FLC that makes the containing statement true.
meaning.note: Supplanted with {{ga ji}} in JACU.

example.lojban: ni'o xu lo prenu co vajni cu {{ge'i}} ca ranji lo nu kansa ku {{gi}} ve'u sepli do gi'e pu co'a cliva fi lo drata se litru
example.english: As for the people important [to you], do they continue to accompany you{{? Or}} are they now distant and separated from you, having departed via their own paths{{?}}
example.author: doriko

gloss: happy, glad — source of happiness

meaning.exp: x_1 is happy/merry/glad/gleeful about x_2 (event/state).

example.lojban: .i lo xanka mutce rirni cu {{gleki}} lo nu lo verba za'o jmive
example.english: The very anxious parents are happy that the child is still alive.
example.author: la solpa'i

example.lojban: .i lo nu jelca cu crori'a ki'u lo nu mi tai {{gleki}} tu'a do
example.english: As they burned it hurt because I was so {{happy}} for you
example.author: Jonathan Coulton

gloss: to work on, worker — to be worked on, work — purpose, goal

meaning.exp: x_1 [person] labors/works on/at x_2 [activity] with goal/objective x_3.
meaning.note: Place structure parallels {{zukte}}.

example.lojban: .i mi {{gunka}} lo se junri cuntu
example.english: I {{am working on}} serious matters!
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

example.lojban: .i la .gregor. cu so'i roi tirna lo nu ra nau zanru {{lo se gunka be lo mensi}}
example.english: Gregor would often hear them say how they appreciated {{the work his sister was doing}}.
example.author: Franz Kafka

example.lojban: .i la cmalu cu {{gunka}} fi tu'a lo cilylarcu
example.english: Tiny {{was working}} on her sewing.
example.note: This sentence can be understood as "Tiny was working, so her sewing [can look good]" (implicit parts in brackets), putting the {{tu'a lo cilylarcu}} in the x_3 place. If the {{tu'a lo cilylarcu}} were in the x_2 place the sentence would mean something like "Tiny was working on [finishing] her sewing".
example.author: la fagri

example.lojban: .i te zu'e lo nu snada {{lo mi te gunka}} kei no stuzi se mau ti maptiu
example.english: For achieving {{my goal}}, no places is better than here.
example.author: Ryūnosuke Akutagawa

gloss: Place Structure: promote other sumti slot to x<sub>1</sub>

meaning.exp: Sumti raising: replaces the meaning of the selbri's original x_1 with "some proposition/event/preperty... involved in x_1". The original x_1 is moved to the {{fai}} place. {{ko'a jai broda}} is equivalent to {{tu'a ko'a (lu'u) broda}}. Used when the selbri takes an abstraction as x_1, but a concrete (object etc.) is desired for the place.
meaning.note: Note that {{jai}} acts on tanru unit (instead of selbri as a whole), so {{jai broda brode}} will have the exact same place strcutre as {{brode}}.

example.lojban: .i mi {{na jai se curmi fai}} lo nu fitytu'i da
example.english: I {{am not allowed to}} let anyone in.
example.author: Brothers Grimm

example.lojban: ni'o {{lo jai daspo}} cu tolcliva
example.english: {{The destroyer}} arrives.
example.author: Robin Lee Powell

example.lojban: .i lo pulji cu {{jai lerci}} dukse
example.english: The police are too {{late}}.
example.note: {{lo pulji}} is <u>not</u> raised in this sentence because {{jai lerci}} is in the seltau (modifying) position of the tanru and thus have no effect on the place strucure of the selbri.
example.author: Unknown

meaning.exp: Replaces the selbri's original x_1 with the sumti introduced by the following preposition. The original x_1 is moved to the {{fai}} place.
meaning.note: Note that {{jai}} acts on tanru unit (instead of selbri as a whole), so {{jai PREPOSITION broda brode}} will have the exact same place strcutre as {{brode}}.

example.lojban: .i {{jai gau sepli fa ko}} {{fai le terdi}} fe le fagri
example.english: {{Separate}} {{the earth}} from the fire.
example.author: an unknown Arabic writer

example.lojban: .i {{lo jai ca cliva}} cu jibni
example.english: {{The hour of his departure}} drew near.
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

example.lojban: .i {{lo jai ja'e dzicatlu be fai py.}} {{lo jai ja'e galcatlu be fai py.}} cu simsa pe'i
example.english: {{The effect to the bird looking down}} would be just the same as to {{that (the effect) of looking up}}.
example.author: Zhuangzi

gloss: Attitudinal (evidential): I conclude

meaning.exp: Evidential: used to express ideas or statements that were not sourced, but rather deduced by the speaker from other sources or statements.

example.lojban: .i {{ja'o}} lo danlu poi xabju lo djacu cu ca'o xabju lo bartu be lo djacu .i ia nai
example.english: {{And it comes to this;}} a creature that lives in water living out of water!
example.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

example.lojban: .i {{ja'o}} mi stidi ru'a lo du'u pilno fi lo ka te cmene kei fe lu jicmu lojbo li'u
example.english: {{Thus,}} I propose that we consequently use the name «Base Lojban» or «Fundamental Lojban».
example.author: la uakci

example.lojban: .i lu {{ja'o}} ma'a ba kavbu lo cifnu li'u
example.english: "{{And therefore}} we shall take babies," [concluded the doctor.]
example.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

gloss: Lojbanist, Lojban user

meaning.exp: x_1 is a Lojbanist.
meaning.note: The place x<sub>2</sub> was defined to be "Lojbanic aspect", but isn't used.

example.lojban: .i ja'o e'o sidju gi'e zukte fi lo xamgu be {{lo balvi jbopre}}
example.english: So, please help and do something for the betterment of {{upcoming Lojbanists}}.
example.author: la solpa'i

gloss: to hold, to grasp — to be held — (of a part of x<sub>1</sub>) to be used for holding ... — (of a part of x<sub>2</sub>) to be held at

meaning.exp: x_1 grasps/holds/clutches/seizes/grips/[hugs] x_2 with x_3 (part of x_1) at locus x_4 (part of x_2).

example.lojban: .i {{bevri jgari}} lo solri lo jgalu
example.english: [He] {{had}} the sun in one claw;
example.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

example.lojban: .i le smani poi se kerlo pa da zi'e noi xendo cu {{jgari}} le cifnu lo birka
example.english: The ape with the one ear, who was a good natured fellow, {{held}} the baby in his arms;
example.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

example.lojban: .i se ni'i bo ra pu'o canci sau lo nu {{tsali jgari fo le mi xance}}
example.english: So before it disappears, [you] need to {{grip my hand tight}}.
example.author: Omoi

gloss: proud, to take pride in ... — pride (something x<sub>1</sub> is proud of)

meaning.exp: x1 (person) feels/has pride in/about x2 (abstraction).

example.lojban: .i to'e mu'i nai {{lo ka jgira}} cu ca to'e ju'o vlipa
example.english: In spite of {{[my] pride}}, [we're] truly powerless...
example.author: Neru

example.lojban: .i lo te pemci ba lo nu se pajni ca lo nu {{jgira lo rigni se cinmo}} cu se dapma gi'e gubni se daspo
example.english: The poet, after a trial, in which {{[he] gloried in his horrid sentiments}}, was condemned and publicly destroyed.
example.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

example.lojban: .i ja'o la'e do'i du {{le se jgira be mi}}
example.english: And this is {{my pride}}.
example.author: an unknown Arabic writer

gloss: Connective: sumti afterthought connective question

meaning.exp: Logical connective: sumti afterthought connective question. Connects two sumti and asks the listener to supply a sumti afterthought connective that makes the containing bridi true.

example.lojban: cacra li re vo pe'i {{ji}} li pa re pei
example.english: Twenty-four hours, I think; {{or}} is it twelve{{?}}
example.author: Lewis Carroll

meaning.exp: Connective: connective question. Connects two grammatical constructs of the same type and asks the listener to supply a connective that makes the containing bridi true.

example.lojban:
― coi jbope'o mi'e zi sipna
― puzi {{ji}} bazi
― naje li'abu'o u'i
example.english:
― Hello Lojban friends, I'm sleeping (from a short distance in time from now)
― To the past {{or}} to the future?
― The latter, should be obvious now, haha.
example.speaker: la srasu, la evis
example.note: The middle sentence would be {{puzi <u>je'i</u> bazi}} under CLL Lojban.

gloss: Attitudinal (discursive): additionally

meaning.exp: Discursive: indicate an additional case or additional cases.
meaning.note: Keywords include "also", "too", "additionally", "in addition", "as well", "moreover", "furthermore", "to boot", "even".

example.lojban: .i lo munje cu palci je'u .i {{ji'a}} lo nu jmive cu nibli lo nu cortu
example.english: The world is truly evil, {{and}} living implies suffering.
example.author: Fyren

gloss: to understand, to comprehend (a fact) — fact understood — subject of understanding

meaning.exp: x_1 understands/comprehends fact/truth x_2 (du'u) about subject x_3; x1 understands (fi) x3.
meaning.note: Place structure parallels that of {{krici}}. Lacks a sumti slot for epistemology/grounds (corresponing to x<sub>4</sub> of {{djuno}}) compared to its near-synonym {{djuno}}.

example.lojban: mi {{jimpe}} lo du'u do ma kau cinmo
example.english: I {{understand}} how you feel.
example.author: L. Frank Baum

example.lojban: .i .a bu snada lo ka {{jimpe}} tu'a lo valsi
example.english: She (Alice) made out the words.
example.note: Make out the words = Succeed to understand the words.
example.author: Lewis Carroll

example.lojban: .i {{jimpe}} fi lo selcni .i .au kelci ne'i le xamsi pe'a
example.english: {{Understanding}} emotions, I want to play in the (figurative) ocean.
example.author: LazuLight

example.lojban: .i do terpa lo nu mi jai gau xrani do se pi'o {{lo se jimpe be mi}}
example.english: You fear that I'll cause harm to you with {{my understandings}}.
example.author: Robin Lee Powell

gloss: to opine, to hold (an opinion) — opinion — subject of opinion — basis/grounds of opinion

meaning.exp: x_1 thinks/opines x_2 [opinion] (du'u) is true about subject/issue x_3 on grounds x_4.
meaning.note: Place structure parallels that of {{djuno}}. Has an additional sumti slot for epistemology/grounds (x<sub>4</sub>) compared to its near-synonym {{krici}}.

example.lojban: lo patfu cu {{jinvi}} fi gy. fe lo du'u mapti fa lo po'o traji jursa
example.english: [...] his father {{thought}} it fitting to always be extremely strict with him.
example.author: Franz Kafka

example.lojban: ni'o mi {{jinvi}} fo lo se junri fe lo du'u lo plini poi terdi lo cmalu noltru cu me lo plinycma po'u li B612
example.english: I have serious reason {{to believe}} that the planet from which the little prince came is the asteroid known as B-612.
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

example.lojban: ni'o vajni lo nabmi fa lo za'i {{lo se jinvi be fi lo du'u ma kau jbobau ku ku}} frica simxu
example.english: The relevant part of this problem is the difference of {{opinions on what is considered a Lojban}}.
example.note: Using two {{ku}} consecutively, as in this sentence, is considered by most to be poor style because it can be difficult to determine which grammatical structure each {{ku}} closes. In this sentence, replacing the two {{ku}} with a {{cu}} keeps the same sentence structure and reduces the cognitive load of backtracking.
example.author: la uakci

gloss: to control, to harness, to direct — to be controlled — controlled action/activity/property

meaning.exp: x_1 has control over/harnesses/manages/directs/conducts x_2 in x_3 (activity/event/performance).

example.lojban: .i ba'a mi ze'e {{se jitro do}} po'o
example.english: My [soul] will always {{be}} only {{yours}}
example.author: José María Lacalle García

example.lojban: .i mu'i bo mi platu lo nu {{jitro}} cy. tai tu'a lo xirma gi'e gasnu lo nu cy. cu gunka
example.english: ..., for I have a mind to {{harness}} him like a horse, and make him work.
example.author: L. Frank Baum

example.lojban: cedra lo nu lo'e cnino joi lo'e citno cu nitcu lo ka {{ce'u kau jitro}} lo jbobau joi lo kulnu pe ri lo ka farvi je lo ka banro
example.english: It's an era in which newcomers and young people need to {{be the directors of}} Lojban and its culture, shaping how it evolves and grows.
example.speaker: la solpa'i
example.note: This sentence is in JACU. To convert it to CLL/BPFK Lojban, substitute {{je}} with {{.e}}.

gloss: to pay attention to, to mind, attentive — focus of attention

meaning.exp: x_1 is attentive towards/attends/tends/pays attention to object/affair x_2.

example.lojban: .i ko {{jundi}} le mi selsa'a
example.english: {{Pay attention}} to my song!
example.author: Kessoku Band

example.lojban: .i ca lo cabna cedra na prali fi lo nu {{na jundi}} tu'a lo bangu klesi
example.english: In the current times, there's no use in {{ignoring}} the dialects.
example.author: la uakci

gloss: Preposition (tense): innate capability

meaning.exp: Innate capability: signifies an innate or potential capability that may or may not be present at the moment due to certain conditions.
meaning.note: Innate capability is unrelated to the condition present at the moment. From BPFK Sections (without the Lojban parts): "[B]irds (except for few species) can fly but among them there are some that cannot do so now due to being crippled, too young, confined in small cage, etc."

example.lojban: .i va'i ro da poi {{ka'e se cusku}}
example.english: That is, all that {{is able to be expressed}}.
example.author: Jorge Luis Borges

example.lojban: .i co'a lo me ru crisa mi do jorne {{lo na ka'e se katna}}
example.english: Starting that summer you and me were connected by {{something that can't be cut apart}}.
example.note: The {{co'a}} follows the BPFK interpretation.
example.author: Djemynai

meaning.exp: Actual capability: signifies capability present at the moment.
meaning.note: Under this meaning, {{x<sub>1</sub> ka'e SELBRI x<sub>2</sub> x<sub>3</sub> ...}} is usually synonymous with {{x<sub>1</sub> kakne lo ka (ce'u) SELBRI x<sub>2</sub> x<sub>3</sub> ...}}.

example.lojban: ni'o le barda prenu ku zukte fi lo nu le cmalu ractu ku {{na ka'e cliva}}
example.english: The big person made it so that the small rabbit {{was unable to leave}}.
example.author: la lalxu

meaning.exp: Possibility: signifies the bridi is possible to be true.

example.lojban: {{ka'e ku}} lo prurai dinsauru cu cti'omni bu'u lo berti bolxadba
example.english: First dinosaurs {{may}} have been omnivores in the north hemisphere
example.source: First dinosaurs may have been omnivores in the north hemisphere
example.author: Chelsea Whyte on NewScientist

meaning.exp: This usage is undefined and not attested.
meaning.note: Mentioned once in roljbogu'e, where {{ka'e SUMTI}} is said to mean "possibility/capability under conditions of SUMTI".

gloss: to be able to — (of an event) possible, (an) ability — condition of possibility/ability

meaning.exp: x_1 is able to do/be/capable of doing/being x_2 (event/state) under conditions x_3 (event/state).

example.lojban: .i flegau fi lo kabri djacu lo kevna be lo kumfa .i lo tsiju cu {{kakne}} lo ka bloti kei lo ka go'i
example.english: Pour a cup of water into a depression in a room, then a seed can be a boat.
example.note: The first sentence is the condition of the second, as seen in the {{lo ka go'i}} as the second sentence's x_3.
example.author: Zhuangzi

example.lojban: ki'e .i mi {{kakne}} lo nu tcidu de'u kei lo nu na sidju
example.english: Thanks, I {{can}} read it without help.
example.speaker: la bakre'u

example.lojban: .i la'e di'u {{na se kakne}}
example.english: That's {{impossible}}.
example.author: Terry Bisson

example.lojban: .i xy. nurgau xy. {{ta'i lo se kakne}}
example.english: They reassure themselves {{as best they can}}.
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

gloss: together, companion, to accompany, to be with ... — to be accompanied — event/condition experienced together

meaning.exp: x_1 is with/accompanies/is a companion of x_2, in state/condition/enterprise x_3 (event/state).
meaning.note: The x<sub>1</sub> and x<sub>2</sub> need not be animate.

example.lojban: .i {{kansa}} lo selnei lo nu ve'u cadzu kei
example.english: {{Accompanying}} [people I] like, walking through a great distance
example.author: doriko

example.lojban: .i lo re moi co'a {{kansa}} lo pa moi {{lo nu se mixre}}
example.english: ..., the second {{mingling with}} the first, ...
example.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

example.lojban: .i se ki'u bo {{ko za'u re'u kansa mi}} ca lo nu mi jai zu'e xabju lo vi daplu fai lo danlu
example.english: So {{join me next time}}, where I’ll populate this island with animals.
example.author: Worldbuilding Notes

gloss: to capture, to seize, to catch — to be captured, to be caught — to be used to capture ..., tool for capture

meaning.exp: x_1 captures/catches/apprehends/seizes/nabs x_2 with trap/restraint x_3.

example.lojban: .i dy. tai certu lo nu {{kavbu}} lo smacu
example.english: ..., and she's such a capital one for {{catching}} mice.
example.author: Lewis Carroll

example.lojban: .i je ba zi bo la selna'i smani cu {{kavbu}} lo vo litru .e .la totos. lo birka gi'e to'o bevri voikla
example.english: ..., and at once the Winged Monkeys {{caught}} the four travelers and Toto up in their arms and flew away with them.
example.author: L. Frank Baum

gloss: to play, player — game, plaything, toy

meaning.exp: x_1 [agent] plays with plaything/toy x_2.
meaning.note: The meaning of "to play (a musical instrument)" is attested (most notably in The Metamorphosis), but is dated (last attested in 2018) and sometimes proscribed. Despite the jbovlaste definition, the x2 is most commonly intepreted as "game". The x2 is generally a descriptive sumti and rarely an abstraction.

example.lojban: .i ko zgana le nu le mlatu cu {{kelci}} le kelproga
example.english: Watch this cat {{playing}} the video game.
example.speaker: yeet kitty

example.lojban: .i {{kelci}} lo nu gismu ke pixra smadi
example.english: [We're] {{playing}} "guessing gismu from pictures".
example.speaker: misotanni
example.note: A rare occasion of an event being in the x<sub>2</sub> of {{kelci}}. Judging from the conversation around it, the game seems to have rules of "one person draws a picture, and others try to guess what gismu it represents", and it is played on skribbl.io.

example.lojban: lo cnino tadji cu {{se kelci}} se mau lo nu nandu se troci
example.english: The new method {{was}} more {{of a game}} than an effort.
example.author: Franz Kafka

gloss: Attitudinal (discursive): again, repeating

meaning.exp: Express that the content is the same as that of something previously expressed.

example.lojban: ca'o ku zo'i sai lo cmana co kasakasas tricypezli cu cadzu fa re citno nanmu [...] .i {{ke'u}} zo'i sai nenri lo cmana
example.english: Two young gentlemen were trekking through fallen leaves deep in the mountains. [...] They {{really}} were very deep in the mountains.
example.note: This example uses CBM, where {{kasakasas}} functions as a brivla. The latter sentence (the one with {{ke'u}}) repeats the former sentence to reinforce the idea that "they were very deep in the mountains".
example.author: Kenji Miyazawa

meaning.exp: Express that something is different from something expressed earlier.

example.lojban: .i {{ke'u nai}} loi djacu cu na rotsu i na ja ri na'e vlipa lo nu sarji lo barda bloti
example.english: If water doesn't have sufficient depth, it will not have strength to support a large boat.
example.note: The text uses many different metaphors to allude to the same idea, with each metaphor being several sentences long. This example sentence is the start of a new metaphor, so it expresses something different from the preceding sentences.
example.author: Zhuangzi

gloss: Attitudinal (discursive): metalinguistic confusion

meaning.exp: Discursive: indicates textual/linguistic/metalinguistic confusion.
Said when the speaker fails to make sense of the text received because of grammaitcal errors, unfamiliar grammatical structures or unfamiliar expressions/words.

example.lojban:
— .i du'u du po tcica
— {{ki'a}}
example.speaker: melody!, Lucilla
example.note: The first sentence is ungrammatical under CLL/BPFK Lojban, and means literally "[It's] the fact that it is [an act of] deceiving" under jboponei, although it's unclear if it's the intended meaning.

example.lojban:
— xu do skalduna?
— .i na go'i .i ku'i mi ca'o cilre lo skara .iu .i mi na'e certu
— skara {{ki'a}} .i skari xu?
example.english:
— Are you Basque?
— No, but I'm learning skara <3 I'm not fluent
— "skara"{{?}} Do you mean "skari"?
example.speaker: Haze, la piier

example.lojban:
— .i ca lo cabdei .i zo'ei mi mo'u te mrilu lo re pi'e re pi'e re pi'e re mei kubli se namkei vau .uisai.u'e
— {{ki'a}} re pi'e re pi'e re pi'e re .i xu ta vonselcimde kubli
example.english:
— Today, I received an 2×2×2×2-cube puzzle by mail :D
— 2×2×2×2{{?}} Is it a four-dimensional cube?
example.speaker: la ziren, qimar

meaning.exp: Said when the speaker encounters a word or a grammatical construction whose referent is unknown.

example.lojban:
— .i .ei do zukte lo do se nupre —sei lo cmalu noltru noi za'ure'u zutse ti'a mi cu nalylau cusku
— .i lo {{ki'a}} se nupre
example.english:
"You must keep your promise," said the little prince, softly, as he sat down beside me once more.
"{{What}} promise?"
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

gloss: Preposition: because of reason ...

meaning.exp: Because of reason ...; Introduces an unnumbered sumti that plays the role of {{krinu}}'s x<sub>1</sub> in the sentence.
meaning.note: The event described by the bridi occurs for the reason indicated by the referent of the tagged sumti.

example.lojban: .i mi'a zukte lo se bilga {{ki'u lo nu kakne}}
example.english: We do what we must {{because we can}}.
example.author: Jonathan Coulton

example.lojban: .i ku'i je'u ty. na'e darsi lo nu darxi la dorotis kei {{ki'u tu'a lo barna be lo mebri}}
example.english: But, in truth, she did not dare to strike Dorothy, {{because of the mark upon her forehead}}.
example.author: L. Frank Baum

meaning.exp: Reasonably therefore ...; Introduces an unnumbered sumti that plays the role of {{krinu}}'s x<sub>2</sub> in the sentence.
meaning.note: The event described by the bridi is the reason behind the event described by the referent of the tagged sumti.

example.lojban: .i xu .iaru'e lu'a lo sfani cu cmacma {{seki'u lo nu lo'e sfani darxi catra tutci cu na plixau}}
example.english: Is it that (I slightly believe) the flies are so small {{the reason that flyswatters aren't useful}}?
example.speaker: niftg

gloss: to cry, to weep — tear — reason of crying, to be cried about

meaning.exp: x_1 weeps/cries tears x_2 about/for reason x_3 (event/state).

example.lojban: .i se ki'u bo ro jabyboi cu binxo {{lo se klaku}}
example.english: And then the little bells are changed to {{tears}}.
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

example.lojban: .i ko na {{klaku fi le marji}}
example.english: Don't {{cry for that material existence}}.
example.author: Noise and Bells (la janbe)

gloss: to go, to come — destination — origin, start — route — means of movement

meaning.exp: x_1 comes/goes to destination x_2 from origin x_3 via route x_4 using means/vehicle x_5.

example.lojban: mi {{klama}} .ii le tsani le mi munje be lo xrani
example.english: I'm scared, but I'm {{going}} to the sky away from my world full of trauma
example.author: Noise and Bells (la janbe)

example.lojban: .i le karce zo'a {{flecu klama}} fo le dargu pe le bartu noi ca'o manku binxo
example.english: Cars {{slushed}} by on the street outside, where it was getting dark.
example.author: Raymond Carver

example.lojban: .i mi {{klama fu}} le roldepre'e .a'o
example.english: I hope I can {{ride}} the local train still.
example.note: {{roldepre'e}} expands to {{ro denpa trene}}, Train that stops at every [station] = Local train.
example.author: inabakumori

example.lojban: .i ku'i mi se slabu lo go'i po'o {{ve klama}}
example.english: But I'm only familiar with said {{route}}.
example.author: la blutolpinxe

gloss: to scream, to yell, to cry out — (a) scream

meaning.exp: x_1 cries out/yells/howls sound x_2; x_1 is a crier.

example.lojban: .i ba bo sutra {{krixa}} zo go'i gi'e troci lo ka cliva
example.english: Then, it quickly {{squeaked}} "yup!" and tried to run away.
example.author: la lalxu

example.lojban: .i lu voksa lo danlu li'u cu se cusku lo krati se pi'o lo voksa poi mutce mleca {{lo se krixa be lo mamta}} lo ka cladu
example.english: "That was the voice of an animal", said the chief clerk, with a voice that was much less loud than {{his mother's scream}}.
example.author: Franz Kafka

gloss: to span, to extend over — range, scope, extent

meaning.exp: x_1 ranges/extends/spans/persists/reaches across/over interval/gap/area/scope/extent/range x_2.

example.lojban: .i lo blanu cu se jetnu skari ra .i je'i ra darno gi'e {{kuspe ve'u fe'e za'o}}
example.english: Is its azure the proper colour? Or is it occasioned by its distance and {{illimitable extent}}?
example.author: Zhuangzi

example.lojban: .i ko'a {{birka kuspe}} le toknu gi'e jai rinka le nu lei ko'a xance cu tagji le cifnu
example.english: He {{reached across}} the stove and tightened his hands on the baby.
example.author: Raymond Carver

example.lojban: .i mi mi punji {{lo se kuspe be py.}}
example.english: I would bring myself down to {{his level}}. (lit. I would put myself within {{his range}}.)
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

gloss: Article: the one(s) called...

meaning.exp: Name article. Converts a selbri, selecting its first argument, or any string of cmevla into a sumti.
meaning.note: The resulting expression refers specifically to an individual or individuals that the speaker has in mind and which the speaker names with the selbri or cmevla.

example.lojban: coi {{la na'e vajni ku}} noi je'a vajni
example.english: Hello {{Not Important}}, who is indeed important!
example.note: "Not Important" is the name of the person greeted. Note the {{ku}} in this expression: it closes the selbri name. if the {{ku}} wasn't there the name selbri becomes {{na'e vajni noi je'a vajni}}, in which the relative clause becomes part of the name.
example.speaker: Lucilla

example.lojban:
— .i ma jmina le jugbau jufra le kibypapri
— {{la .lukifer.kailus.delikatus.}} no'u {{la .yu'orb.}}
example.english:
— Who added the Chiese sentences to the webpage?
— {{Lucifer Caelius Delicatus}} a.k.a. {{Yuorb}}
example.note: Specifically chosen to showcase cmevla chaining, where multiple cmevla in a row functions as a single name. Also note the answer parses differently in regards to CBM: with CBM {{.lukifer.kailus.delikatus. no'u la .yu'orb.}} is a name; without CBM {{no'u la .yu'orb.}} is a relative phrase of {{la .lukifer.kailus.delikatus.}} signifying the equivalence between them. Also note {{yu'orb}} is not a standard Lojban cmevla because of the {{y}}.
example.speaker: la nalvai, la ilmen

meaning.context: when used with an inner quantifier
meaning.exp: The inner quantifier signifies the number of the referents the speaker has in mind. If no explicit inner quantifier is supplied, it defaults to {{su'o}}.
meaning.note: {{la}} is seldom used with quantifiers.

meaning.context: when used with an inner quantifier
meaning.exp: The inner quantifier is part of the name.
meaning.note: {{la}} is seldom used with quantifiers. The following example is the only instance of {{la}} with inner quantifier I found.

example.lojban: mi pu finti {{la ze tadji pe lu mi prami do li'u}} te zu'e lo nu loi se cinri cu kakne lo ka troci lo ka smucpa
example.english: I authored {{Seven Ways to Say "I Love You"}} so that those interested can try to get its meaning.
example.speaker: la solpa'i
example.note: "Seven Ways to Say 'I Love You'" probably refers to a set of seven sentences in Toaq. The quote is from June 2017, so the Toaq is supposedly not too distant from that.

gloss: Quotation: start non-Lojban quotation as name

meaning.exp: Begin non-Lojban name. The next Lojban word loses all its grammatical function, becomes the quote delimiter, and quotes all further text until the same word is repeated. The quote delimiters and the quoted text must be separated with pauses. The entire construct (from {{la'o}} to the second delimiter) is a sumti meaning "that named <quoted text>", and is considered a single word for grammatical purposes.
meaning.note: The delimiter is usually chosen to give hints to the nature of the quoted text. For example, the first letter of the source language. {{zoi}} is often used as the default delimiter if no hints is to be given (in which case the construct is {{la'o zoi. <quoted text> .zoi}}).

example.lojban: ni'o ti datni papri fi'e {{la'o gy. blinry .gy.}} fi'o plijaspu {{la'o gy. CC0 .gy.}}
example.english: Cheat sheet by {{blinry}}, (with license) {{CC0}}.
example.author: Blinry

example.lojban: ni'o salci {{la'o zoi León Werth zoi}} pe ca lo nu ly. verba
example.english: To {{León Werth}} when he was a little boy
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

gloss: Quotation: end ungrammatical/out-of-context/sentence fragment quotation

meaning.exp: End error quotation. Ends a questionable or out of context quotation. Never elidable.

example.lojban: .i lo'u lan lan la lan la la la la lan lan la lan la la la la lan lan la la lan la la la lan la la la la lan o'o'o'o'o'o'o'o'o'o lun lun lu lu'u'u'u'u'u lu lu lu lu lun lu lu lu lun lu {{le'u}}
example.author: Youmi Kimura

example.lojban: .i do lo'u .i lo mi panzi lo mi speni {{le'u}} .alcu do lo'u zo'u mo {{le'u}}
example.english: "My kids... my wife,{{"}} you said. "What about them?{{"}}
example.note: The entire sentence is grammatical, but becomes ungrammatical when split in half.
example.author: Andy Weir

gloss: Mekso: forms number, convert methematical expression to sumti

meaning.exp: Number. It converts a mathematical or numerical expression (MEX) into a sumti. The sumti refers to the value of the numerical expression. It is usually a numerical value, but it may be any referent of a numerical expression, for example a date. Terminate with {{lo'o}}.

example.lojban: .i ca ku .abu {{centre li so'u re mu}}
example.english: ..., she was now {{only ten inches}} [high], ...
example.note: The Lojban example translates literally to "... only 25 centimeters", as ten inches is about 25 centimeters. Combining definite and indefinite numbers into a single number implies that the two kinds of numbers have the same value in the given context (CLL 18.8), as seen in the {{so'u re mu}} in this example, where the {{re mu}} is taken to have the same value of {{so'u}} (few), thus the translation of "only 25".
example.author: Lewis Carroll

example.lojban: .i .e'o pensi ~ mi'e la uakci to'i de'i {{li re no pa ze ny pa ly mu dy}}
example.english: Please [take some time to] consider this! ~ la uakci, {{January 5, 2017}}
example.note: The mathematical expression is taken as a date. The {{ny}}, {{ly}}, {{dy}} stand for year, month, day respectively.
example.author: la uakci

example.lojban: .i ku'i simlu lo ka sisku fi tu'a le daski kei ja'e le nu ti'u {{li pa ci pi'e re no vu'u pi'e pi'e dau}} cu klama le jai purci te zu'e tu'a le nalvai gluta pe le nei
example.english: Wait a second, looks like he's looking for something in his pockets and at {{thirteen twenty minus ten seconds}} he goes back in for his crummy gloves.
example.note: The mathematical expression is taken as a time.
example.author: Szymborska Wisława

gloss: Attitudinal (discursive): obviously, clearly

meaning.exp: Express obviousness. Indicates that the speaker regards the referent of the construct as obvious.

example.lojban: .i {{li'a}} mi na certu lo ka sanga
example.english: {{Obviously}} I'm not good at singing.
example.author: Djemynai

example.lojban: .i no da poi na xabju lo djacu cu kakne lo nu te sidbo lo temci .e {{ji'a li'a}} lo junla
example.english: No one not living in water could conceive the idea of time, {{how much less of}} a clock!
example.author: Robert Louis Stevenson

example.lojban: .i mi to'e ri'a nai snada .i {{li'a dai}} go'i
example.english: Despite [all that] I succeeded (It {{should be obvious to you}})
example.author: la solpa'i

meaning.exp: Express obscureness. Indicates that the speaker regards the referent of the construct as obscure (ie. difficult to understand).

example.lojban: .i li'a mi na dunli pilno ro lo cumki jbogerna noi cimni {{li'a nai pei}}
example.english: Obviously I don't use all possible Lojban grammar equally, which are infinite, {{isn't it hard to understand?}}
example.speaker: la lunbe

gloss: Quotation: start ungrammatical/out-of-context/sentence fragment quotation

meaning.exp: Begin error quotation. Starts a questionable or out of context quotation. Text must be Lojban words, but needn't be grammatical. Terminate with {{le'u}}.

example.lojban: .i {{lo'u}} lan lan la lan la la la la lan lan la lan la la la la lan lan la la lan la la la lan la la la la lan o'o'o'o'o'o'o'o'o'o lun lun lu lu'u'u'u'u'u lu lu lu lu lun lu lu lu lun lu le'u
example.author: Youmi Kimura

example.lojban: .i do {{lo'u}} .i lo mi panzi lo mi speni le'u .alcu do {{lo'u}} zo'u mo le'u
example.english: {{"}}My kids... my wife," you said. {{"}}What about them?"
example.note: The entire sentence is grammatical, but becomes ungrammatical when split in half.
example.author: Andy Weir

gloss: suitable, to match, to fit — what x<sub>1</sub> matches, what x<sub>1</sub> is suitable for — aspect/property where x<sub>1</sub> fits

meaning.exp: x_1 fits/matches/suits/is compatible/appropriate/corresponds to/with x_2 in property/aspect x_3.

example.lojban: .i lu mi na fengu li'u co'u {{mapti}} lo fatci
example.english: The sentence "I'm not angry" no longer {{matches}} the actualities.
example.author: Mèremim

example.lojban: za'a dai mi na'e ke clira {{mapti}} fi lo ka kelci
example.english: As you can see, I'm not {{suitable}} for playing [because it's] too late [here now].
example.speaker: la uakci
example.note: The main selbri, {{clira mapti}}, translated literally to "early-suitable", which is taken to be "be early enough to be suitable" in the translation given above.

gloss: million, millions of ... — unit (of millions), to form millions, to make up millions

meaning.exp: x_1 is a million [10<sup>6</sup>] of x_2 in dimension/aspect x_3 (default is units).

example.lojban: .i ze'u lo nanca be {{lo megdo}} lo xrula cu zbasu lo kinli
example.english: The flowers have been growing thorns for {{millions}} of years.
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

example.lojban: .i lo nu ra fengu je jusycurve lumci cu rinka lo nalracli nu cirko {{lo megdo be lo cukta}}
example.english: It is their rage-fueled and fundamentalist cleansing that caused the senseless loss of {{millions of volumes}}.
example.author: Jorge Luis Borges

gloss: beautiful, pretty — to find beautiful, to find pretty — beautiful aspect — beauty standard

meaning.exp: x_1 is beautiful/pleasant to x_2 in aspect x_3 (ka) by aesthetic standard x_4.

example.lojban:
— .i grusi blanu ca .i {{melbi}} mi .i xu lo do tsani cu {{melbi}} do
— .i {{melbi}} mi lo ka dilnu claxu blanu
example.english:
— It's grayish blue now. It's {{beautiful}} to me. Is your sky {{beautiful}} to you?
— It's {{beautiful}} to me in that it's blue without clouds.
example.speaker: la lunbe, niftg

example.lojban: .i pe'i ro bangu cu {{melbi fi da}}
example.english: I think every language {{is beautiful in some ways}}.
example.speaker: la xrula

example.lojban: .i ku'i mi {{se melbi}} le do ganto'a sai voksa
example.english: But I {{find}} your very deep voice {{beautiful}}.
example.speaker: la janbe

gloss: mild, somewhat, a little ..., a bit ... — a mild property

meaning.exp: x_1 is mild/non-extreme/gentle/middling/somewhat in property x_2 (ka); x_1 is not very x_2.
meaning.note: Lacks a sumti slot for direction of mildness (corresponing to x<sub>3</sub> of {{mutce}}) compared to its antonym {{mutce}}.

example.lojban: .i la saix. jundi gi'e {{milxe lo ka jimpe}}
example.english: Sai listened and {{understood a little}}.

example.lojban: .i je lo ji'a sai pilka cu {{crino milxe}}
example.english: And even [his] skin {{was of a greenish tint}}.
example.author: L. Frank Baum

gloss: cat — breed/species of cat

meaning.exp: x_1 is a cat/[puss/pussy/kitten] [feline animal] of species/breed x_2; (adjective:) x_1 is feline.
meaning.note: Usage of x<sub>2</sub> is not attested, though the place is mentioned quite often when discussing type-semantics of Lojban.

example.lojban: ju'o la .dinas. ca lo cabnicte ba mutce lo ka claxu mi to sa'a la .dinas. {{cu mlatu}} toi
example.english: Dinah will miss me very much tonight, I should think! (Dinah {{was the cat}}.)
example.author: Lewis Carroll

example.lojban: .i la .totos. pu bajra se ka'a lo midju be lo remgunma te zu'e lo nu gercmo fa'a {{lo citno mlatu}}
example.english: Toto had run into the crowd to bark at {{a kitten}}.
example.author: L. Frank Baum

gloss: Selbri question

meaning.exp: Asks the listener to supply a selbri that makes the containing bridi true.
meaning.note: As the meaning of this word is really broad, it has many possible translations in English, each with a more specific meaning than {{mo}}. Which translation applies depends on context.

example.lojban: lo se citka ku {{mo}}
example.english: {{What happened to}} the stuff I was going to eat?
example.author: la lalxu

example.lojban: .i le se cradi .e le notci be fo lo tarci cu {{mo}}
example.english: {{What about}} the radio signals? The messages to the stars?
example.author: Terry Bisson

example.lojban: .i xy. to'e lazni gunka co'a lo cerni co'u lo nicte gi'e na djuno lo du'u lo si'o gleki cu {{mo kau}}
example.english: He worked hard from morning till night and did not know {{what}} joy {{was}}.
example.author: L. Frank Baum

example.lojban: .i {{do mo}} lo tarci
example.english: And {{what do you do with}} these stars?
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

example.lojban: lo {{mo}} prenu cu xabju lo vi sruri
example.english: {{What sort of}} people live about here?
example.note: An example of {{mo}} used as a tanru unit.
example.author: Lewis Carroll

gloss: to remember — memory, (of a fact) to be remembered — subject of memory, (of a object, person) to be remembered

meaning.exp: x_1 remembers/recalls/recollects fact(s)/memory x_2 (du'u) about subject x_3.
meaning.note: Place structure parallels that of {{jimpe}}.

example.lojban: .i mi pu tcidu di'u lo cukta .i ku'i mi {{na morji lo du'u cy. mo kau}}
example.english: I've read that in some book, but I {{don't remember where}}.
example.author: Lewis Carroll

example.lojban: .i ku'i lo prenu cu {{prami morji fi la .oz.}} gi'e simxu lo ka cusku
example.english: But the people {{remembered him (= Oz) lovingly}}, and said to one another.
example.author: L. Frank Baum

example.lojban: {{le se morji be mi}} cu mutce le ka kalsa
example.english: {{My memories}} are very confused.
example.author: H. P. Lovecraft

example.lojban: .i mi troci lo ka skicu py. vau te zu'e lo ka na {{to'e morji fi py.}}
example.english: I try to describe him to make sure that I shall not {{forget him}}.
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

gloss: dead

meaning.exp: x_1 is dead/has ceased to be alive.

example.lojban: .i {{lo morsi}} na ka'e pensi
example.english: {{Dead ones}} cannot think.
example.author: la blutolpinxe

example.lojban: .i se ki'u bo ba'e mo va'o lo nu lo remna cu rivbi cliva troci pu {{lo nu ry morsi}}
example.english: so what if humans tried to escape the egg before {{they all died}}?
example.author: Worldbuilding Notes

example.lojban: .i go'i se va'u ro ma'a {{poi ke'a na morsi ca}}
example.english: For the good of all of us, {{except the ones who are dead}}
example.author: Jonathan Coulton

gloss: Preposition: because of motive ...

meaning.exp: Because of motive ...; Introduces an unnumbered sumti that plays the role of {{mukti}}'s x<sub>1</sub> in the sentence.
meaning.note: The event described by the bridi occurs because of the motive described by the referent of the tagged sumti.

example.lojban: .i ba ku {{mu'i lo nu tatpi}} cu cpana lo ckana
example.english: And then [she] lied on a bed {{because [she] was tired}}.
example.author: Brothers Grimm

example.lojban: .i vy. xaksu lo temci {{mu'i tu'a lo bukpu selkeipre}}
example.english: They waste their time {{over a rag doll}} [...]
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

meaning.exp: Motive therefore ...; Introduces an unnumbered sumti that plays the role of {{mukti}}'s x<sub>2</sub> in the sentence.
meaning.note: The event described by the bridi is the motive behind the event described by the referent of the tagged sumti.

example.lojban: .i mi tolnei lo'e morna kibystu {{semu'i lonu zbasu lo narpanra}}
example.english: I dislike template websites in general, {{so [I] build something unique}}.
example.speaker: latkerlo

meaning.exp: Motive of person ...; Introduces an unnumbered sumti that plays the role of {{mukti}}'s x<sub>3</sub> in the sentence.
meaning.note: Unattested.
meaning.noshownote: There is a usage, {.i lo da'i nu do da viska cu mukti fi ko fe lo nu cusku no da gi'e pinxe te mu'i lo nu co'u morji} (jbobratca chatlog), in which the {te mu'i} seems like an error for {te zu'e}.

gloss: motive, incentive, (of an event) to motivate — (of an event) to be done because of motive ... — to be motivated to ...

meaning.exp: x_1 (action/event/state) motivates/is a motive/incentive for action/event x_2, per volition of x_3.

example.lojban: .i ku'i mi jimpe {{lo mukti be lo nu mi za'o troci}}
example.english: but I understand {{the reason why I'm still trying}},
example.author: Noise and Bells

example.lojban: .i mi {{te mukti}} lo nu vofli kei lo nu galtu klama
example.english: I {{set my mind on}} flying to reach high.
example.author: Zhuangzi

example.lojban: .i ri {{te mukti fi}} lo nu fekydji lo nu cpacu lo cukta pe la conxunre xavyselmla
example.english: They {{were spurred on by}} the zeal to reach the books of the Crimson Hexagon.
example.author: Jorge Luis Borges

gloss: extreme, much, very — an extreme property

meaning.exp: x_1 is much/extreme in property x_2 (ka), towards x_3 extreme/direction; x_1 is, in x_2, very x_3.
meaning.note: Has an additional sumti slot for direction of extremeness (x<sub>3</sub>) compared to its antonym {{milxe}}.

example.lojban: le se morji be mi cu {{mutce}} le ka kalsa
example.english: My memories are {{very}} confused.
example.author: H. P. Lovecraft

example.lojban: .i cu'u so'e se slabu be mi mi {{mutce be fi tu'a lo mi se nanca be'o}} mencre
example.english: Most people who are familiar with me say I'm {{really}} smart {{for my age}}.
example.author: la blutolpinxe

example.lojban: .i ja'e bo ca ku mi {{cinmo lo mutce}} gi'e kakne co zukte no da
example.english: As a result I {{am overwhelmed}} and cannot do anything now.
example.speaker: la nalvai
example.note: To be overwhelmed = To feel an extreme emotion

gloss: (of an event, activity) difficult, to be difficult to ... — to find ... difficult — (of a situation/condition) to make it difficult for ...

meaning.exp: x_1 is difficult/hard/challenging for x_2 under conditions x_3; x_1 challenges (non-agentive) x_2.

example.lojban: .i {{nandu}} fa lo ka du'eski lo mi nunmansa
example.english: {{It's hard to}} overstate my satisfaction
example.author: Jonathan Coulton

example.lojban: .i so'i cnima'o cu fanva {{jai nandu}}
example.english: Many attitudinals {{are difficult}} to translate.
example.note: The {{so'i cnima'o}} is raised with {{jai}} since {{nandu}} takes abstraction (event, etc.) as x<sub>1</sub>.
example.speaker: la lunbe

example.lojban: ni'o lo ralju be {{lo nandu be la .alis.}} ca lo cfari cu nu jitro lo fagycpi
example.english: The chief {{difficulty Alice found}} at first was in managing her flamingo.
example.author: Lewis Carroll

example.lojban: .i ru'a {{nandu fi}} lonu smuvrici
example.english: I assume it{{'s hard when}} it's ambiguous.
example.speaker: la melmi

gloss: to like, fond — to be liked

meaning.exp: x_1 is fond of/likes/has a taste for x_2 (object/state).

example.lojban: .i mi {{nelci}} ro selci be do
example.english: I {{like}} every one of your cells.
example.author: Djemynai

example.lojban: .i mi {{nelci}} ca lo nicte lo nu tirna lo tarci
example.english: At night I {{love to}} listen to the stars.
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

example.lojban: ko te cmene fi {{lo do se nelci}}
example.english: Call it {{whatever you like}}.
example.author: Lewis Carroll

gloss: to need — to be needed, necessity, something necessary — (of an event, goal) to require

meaning.exp: x_1 needs/requires/is dependent on/[wants] necessity x_2 for purpose/action/stage of process x_3.
meaning.note: The x<sub>2</sub> can be either a concrete (person, object, etc.) or an abstraction (event etc.).

example.lojban: .i mi do {{na nitcu}} .i ji'a do mi {{na nitcu}}
example.english: I {{have no need of}} you. And you {{have no need of}} me.
example.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry

example.lojban: .i do lo nu djuno lo du'u ma kau smuvanbi cu {{nitcu}} lo nu jdice lo du'u ma kau smuni
example.english: You'll [often] {{need}} to know the context to decide what things mean.
example.author: Blinry

example.lojban: .i lo nu kansa cu {{se nitcu}} .ie .i ku'i za'a do na djica

meaning.exp: Letteral for o. When used alone, refers to the most recent sumti starting with {{o}}.

meaning.exp: Equivalent to {{.i ko'oi}}. Starts a sentence that is a command.

gloss: Quotation: start non-Lojban quotation

meaning.exp: Begin non-Lojban quotation. The next Lojban word loses all its grammatical function, becomes the quote delimiter, and quotes all further text until the same word is repeated. The quote delimiters and the quoted text must be separated with pauses. The entire construct (from {{zoi}} to the second delimiter) is a sumti meaning "the text <quoted text>", and is considered a single word for grammatical purposes.
meaning.note: The delimiter is usually chosen to give hints to the nature of the quoted text. For example, the first letter of the source language, or {{urli}} when it is an URL. {{zoi}} is often used as the default delimiter if no hints is to be given (in which case the construct is {{zoi zoi. <quoted text> .zoi}}).

example.lojban: .i mu'i gi so'o da te smuni lu kampu bangu li'u {{la'e zoi gy. lingua franca .gy}} gi mi te smuni zo kampu tu'a lo nu le bangu cu jai se pi'o kakne fai lo vrici be tu'a lo jbebau lo ka casnu

gloss: (pedantic) naysayer, to belittle ... by acting pedantic on their grammar, to criticize ...'s grammar without adding to the conversation — to be needlessly criticized for making a grammatical error as perceived by x<sub>1</sub>

meaning.exp: x_1 acts Lojbanically cruel/pedantic toward x_2 in manner x_3 (ka). Refers to a particular, infamous cultural phenomenon in the Lojban community wherein many conversations between speakers in or tangential to Lojban tend to very quickly devolve into an argument over grammar, semantics, or usage, with the result that it becomes difficult if not impossible to hold an ordinary conversation in the language on any subject in forums where this behavior is not explicitly discouraged.
meaning.note: Originally a clipping of {{xekcedipasopa}}, i.e. "XKCD #191," in which R. Munroe observes that Lojban's utility as a means of expression is severely hampered by the fact that speaking it requires you to interact with "the kind of people who learn Lojban." This word has been borrowed in English, as "xekce", which means {{lo xekce}} or {{lo nu xekce}} (depending on context) and shows up very often when talking about Lojban culture. Merely correcting other people's grammar does *not* constitute {{xekce}}. The (infamous) "Glasgow conversation" is the archetypical instance of xekce, where they start talking about something mundane, it lasts for like three sentences before nitcion gets mad and starts lecturing goran about {{bu'u}} (which wasn't accepted as "official" at that time), and then they never get back to the original topic and switch back to english to argue and then goran leaves. Practicing xekce is banned in roljbogu'e. See also here.
meaning.noshownote: This long, long definition and note is taken from jbovlaste and https://discord.com/channels/771781383361921024/771782436807245835/1042853305375785030 from la janbe. How should I credit it?
